For you know the poverty of our see, the difficulty of the roads, the storm of wars, the hatred of the people of Cambrai against us, and the hostility of certain others situated along the route.
>
> “Therefore, prostrate at the feet of your holiness, we humbly beseech you to hear me in the word of truth and to be willing to regard me as excused; and that you may please urge the lord archbishop, opening upon us and upon the Church entrusted to us the bowels of his mercy, to support with his suffrages, according to the tenor of the letters sent him by the lord pope, those same letters. And that you may remove from us every occasion of contempt, we present our profession through these brothers of ours, intending to make the same when, by God’s mercy, we can come to you safely.”

> “To his reverend father and lord Raynold, by the grace of God archbishop of Reims: Lambert, unworthy servant of the holy see of Arras, with the reverence due to submission, sends that which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man.
>
> “Since we have endeavoured, as soon as possible, to send your fatherhood the letters of Lord Pope Urban, together with our own letters containing the causes that prevented us, it seems very hard to us that you have chosen to write nothing to us either in accordance with the tenor of the lord pope’s letters or in answer to the supplication of our letters; but through Hameric, abbot of Anchin—which did not become your gentleness—you sent us letters in which you called us an intruder upon the see of Arras, and commanded that we should not admonish the abbots to obedience to our Church, as the letters sent them by the lord pope require.
>
> “We, however, again endeavoured through the common son of your Church and ours, Lord Hugh, abbot of Saint-Denis, to make known to your discretion the reasons why it is presently impossible for us to come to you. Yet in all these matters we have deserved to receive, neither the first nor the second time, any message from you prompted by merciful affection or any compassion. Instead, through the monks of Marchiennes, on the matter of Lord Alard the archdeacon and of one excommunicated man who died, without confession and viaticum, during an assault on the Church—although otherwise has been reported to you—you sent letters in which you wished to represent us as, in effect, a contemner of the Church of Reims.
>
> “Yet your prudence is not unaware that we did not seize this see beforehand, but acquired it constrained and compelled by obedience to apostolic authority. Therefore, lest I appear in the eyes of your mercy to be a contemner of the holy Church of Reims, we send these brothers of ours to make satisfaction in our person and words on our behalf. We beseech your clemency, then, to receive our profession in the meantime through these present brothers: both for the love of the Holy Spirit and for love and reverence of the lord pope, performing with us a like work of mercy to that which you received from apostolic favour at the time of your own profession.
>
> “When, through God’s mercy, the opportunity to travel to you has been granted, we profess that, God willing, we shall then do in person what we now do through our brothers. We also beseech your fatherhood to support with your suffrages the letters of the lord pope, as he wrote to you. We shall deal kindly, out of love for you, with Lord Alard the archdeacon, the abbots, and their causes, if they obey the lord pope’s letters. Fare ever well in the Lord, reverend father and lord.”

> “I, Lambert, ordained bishop of the see of Arras, promise you, Pastor Raynold, and the privilege of the Church of Reims and your successors, according to the sacred canons and decrees of the Apostolic See promulgated from the sacred canons and laws, that to the extent of my knowledge and ability I shall obey. I also profess that I shall labour with diligence, counsel, and cooperation for the public and private affairs of the same metropolitan; and that without his consent I shall give no assent in major affairs or ordinations, except in matters belonging to my own diocese. To this my profession, before God and his saints and in the presence of this Church as witness, I subscribe in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.”

This profession was made at Reims in September, on 21 September, the feast-day of blessed Matthias, apostle and evangelist, in the second indiction, in the year of Christ 1094.

> “Raynold, by the grace of God archbishop of Reims, to the most glorious prince Lord Robert, count of the Flemings, abundance of salvation and blessing in the Lord.
>
> “We have kindly received and gratefully read the letters of your affection. Since in them you asked us to send word of what we thought concerning the appointment of our most beloved brother Lambert, bishop of Arras, we do not wish your prudence, so dear to us, to be unaware that we detained him for many days, so that what was to be done concerning him might lawfully be done by the counsel of our bishops. At last, at the council which we held at Reims with our fellow bishops and many princes on 17 September, in accordance with the commands of Lord Pope Urban, to disobey which is sinful, we received his profession in the ecclesiastical manner by the counsel and assent of our fellow bishops, and, confirming his consecration, confirmed it.
>
> “We therefore enjoin upon your concern that henceforth you receive him with due honour and due reverence, share publicly and privately in his labours for the love of God, and, insofar as ecclesiastical order permits, obey him as your pastor and bishop. Farewell.”

> “Raynold, by the grace of God archbishop of Reims, to his dearest son Lambert, fellow priest and fellow bishop, that which is his in the Lord.
>
> “Know that we have absolved this canon, namely Engelbert. As for the others who have already come to you, or shall come, on account of our excommunication, we will and command that you also absolve them and strive to place them under regular discipline, where they may receive consolation for body and soul, until their Church comes to its senses; and thus, after our absolution and permission, may receive them as your own sons. Farewell.”

> “Raynold, by the grace of God archbishop of Reims, to his most beloved fellow brother and fellow priest Lambert, bishop of the people of Arras, greetings and blessing in the Lord Jesus.
>
> “We have judged it fitting to notify your affection that we have very recently received a letter from Lord Pope Urban, and that, having summoned your brotherhood, you have been instructed by him to take care to come into his presence about the middle of the coming February at the council which he is then to celebrate somewhere in Tuscany or Lombardy. We therefore, in obedience to his admonition, admonish your brotherhood to take care to present yourself to him at the said time, with all your abbots, at that council. Farewell.”

> “Hugh, archbishop of Lyons, legate of the Apostolic See, to Robert, most noble count of the Flemings, greetings.
>
> “Our venerable brother in Christ, the bishop of Arras,” etc. See under Hugh of Lyons, *Patrologia*, vol. CLVII.

> “Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Walcher, bishop-elect of Cambrai, greetings and apostolic blessing.
>
> “You ought to remember,” etc. See under Urban II, *Patrologia*, vol. CLI.

> “Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Robert, count of the Flemings, and his nobles, greetings and apostolic blessing.
>
> “On behalf of our most dear brother Lambert,” etc. See above.

Accordingly, in the year of Christ 1099, Lord Pope Urban II—who had earlier celebrated a general council at Clermont—again undertook to summon to a council at Rome, in the church of blessed Peter the apostle, the primates, archbishops, and bishops of various regions and provinces, concerning the error and heresies of the Greeks, on the second Sunday after Easter, when *Misericordia Domini* (“The mercy of the Lord”) is sung. Lambert, bishop of Arras, attended this council with the other bishops of the province of Reims. What decrees the aforesaid pope issued before the body of blessed Peter concerning the Latin and Greek Church, ministers of the altar, persons ordained by simoniacs, and ecclesiastical benefices and offices acquired for money, the diligent reader may discover by reading.

Accordingly, in the aforesaid year of Christ 1099, on 29 July, in the seventh indiction, Pope Urban II, a religious man of worthy memory, entered upon the way of all flesh; and he was buried in the church of blessed Peter the apostle, beside Saint Leo the pope and author of the Council of Ephesus. Urban was succeeded in the Apostolic See by Lord Rainer, the venerable cardinal of the title of Saint Clement, surnamed Pope Paschal II.

> “Paschal, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Lambert, bishop of Arras, and his successors canonically appointed for ever.
>
> “Those things which have been justly established by the fathers,” etc. See under Paschal II, *Patrologia*, vol. CLXIII.

> “Paschal, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother Ralph, archbishop of Reims, greetings and apostolic blessing.
>
> “Concerning the restoration of the bishopric of Arras,” etc. See above.

Know that copies of these letters, with their bull, are kept at Reims, in the church of our lady the blessed ever-Virgin Mary, in the treasury, in the little golden chest commonly called the *berceolum*.

> “Paschal, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the clergy and people of Arras, greetings and apostolic blessing.
>
> “We have heard that certain persons act perversely,” etc. See above.

> “Paschal, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Baldwin, count of the Flemings, and to his distinguished mother Countess Clementia, greetings and apostolic blessing.
>
> “Concerning the bishopric of Arras,” etc. See above.

> “Raynold, by the grace of God archbishop of Reims, to his most beloved brother and fellow priest Lambert, bishop of the people of Arras, greetings and blessing in the Lord Jesus.
>
> “We do not wish your brotherhood, most dear to us, to be unaware that we have very recently received a letter from Lord Pope Urban. It has instructed us to come in person to the council which he is to celebrate in the octave of Saint Martin, namely on 18 November, at the church of Auvergne, also called Clermont; and it has commanded us to invite all the suffragans of our metropolitan see to that council, after summoning both the abbots and the other leaders of the Churches, as well as the more eminent princes.
>
> “We, then, unwilling—as would be sinful—to oppose the apostolic admonition, judged that the council which we had planned for the octave of All Saints ought justly to be abandoned for this reason. Therefore, by this letter we admonish your diligence to set aside every excuse, attend the same council in person, and, as said above, take care to summon both the abbots and the leaders of your other Churches, the princes of your diocese, and especially Baldwin, count of Monts.
>
> “Let neither poverty nor any pretext of necessity give anyone boldness to stay away; for we require only persons, not persons attended by a great throng of servants. Whoever, after this admonition of ours, absents himself from this council should undoubtedly know that he shall incur danger to his order and store up for himself the anger of the lord pope—and not with impunity. Farewell.”

> “Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brother Lambert, bishop of Arras, greetings and apostolic blessing.
>
> “Let your affection know,” etc. See under Urban II, *Patrologia*, vol. CLI.

Thus Lambert, bishop of Arras, summoned to the Council of Clermont by Lord Pope Urban, set out on the feast-day of the apostles Simon and Jude, then a Sunday. With him were Lord Clarembald, his archdeacon; the venerable Lord Alold, abbot of Saint-Vaast, and Lord Hameric, abbot of Anchin; Lord Gualbert, provost; Odo, cantor; Achard, master of the schools; Hugh, priest and canon; Mascellin, archpriest; the religious deacon John of Mont-Saint-Éloi, later archdeacon of Arras; Drogo, steward of the said bishop; and Otbert, schoolmaster of Béthune.

Having reached Provins, the celebrated castle of Count Stephen, he left Provins on 6 November. On that very day he was dragged from his road, seized, and, being seized, detained with his clerics by a certain knight Guarnier of the castle of Pont and his retainers. The abbot of Saint-Vaast had gone ahead of the bishop with his leave and blessing. But Guarnier, reproved by his brother Philip, bishop of Troyes, and visited by the mercy of almighty God, early on 9 November threw himself at the feet of the bishop, his archdeacon Clarembald, and his other clerics, seeking pardon with tears. He grieved and repented that he had acted foolishly and wickedly in laying hands on the Lord’s anointed.

The bishop raised the prostrate knight and went ahead of the barefoot knight to the monastery. There he absolved him, as he and those who had seized him performed penance. On the same day the bishop and all his clerics and lay companions were retained, served, and safely conducted by the hand of the aforesaid knight as far as Auxerre. When Lord Pope Urban heard that the bishop of Arras had been captured, he immediately wrote to Guarnier of Pont and to Richer, venerable archbishop of Sens, as follows:

> “Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Guarnier, son of Pont, greetings and apostolic blessing, if he obeys.
>
> “We have heard that you have captured our venerable brother, the bishop of Arras, as he was coming to the council,” etc. See above.

> “Urban, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his dearest brother Richer, archbishop of Sens, greetings and apostolic blessing.
>
> “We have heard that Guarnier, son of Pont, has seized our venerable brother the bishop of Arras as he was coming to the council, and keeps him captive,” etc. See above.

When the bishop of Arras arrived at Auxerre, he joined the company of Lord Richer, archbishop of Sens, and his fellow suffragans from the province of Reims: Lord Gerwin, bishop of Amiens, and Lord Gerard, bishop of Thérouanne. Thus, on 17 November, in the octave of Saint Martin, which that Sunday made more festive, he entered the city of Clermont. He was graciously received with the holy kiss by the venerable primate of Lyons, Lord Hugh, legate of the Apostolic See, and by the lord pope himself; and, gladdened with his companions by the apostolic blessing, he rejoiced.

Then, on 28 November, in the fourth indiction, Lord Pope Urban, concluding the Council of Clermont, commanded that the privilege of the renewal and restoration of the Church of Arras be recited in the sight of the whole council. Roman cardinals sat with him, together with fourteen archbishops, two hundred and twenty-five bishops, and ninety or more abbots, apart from honourable and religious clerics and laymen of diverse regions and provinces, whose number no one could easily know because of their multitude. The privilege of the Church of Arras was recited and read distinctly and clearly; and, under great silence, it was attentively heard, praised, and confirmed by the entire assembly of the council in the year of Christ 1095—to whom, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, belong equal honour and glory through endless ages of ages. Amen.

[Col. 0647]

## II. LETTERS OF LAMBERT, BISHOP OF ARRAS, AND OTHERS TO HIM

(Baluze, *Miscellanea*, Luc. edition in folio, II, 137.)

### LETTER I. WALTER, PROVOST OF LILLE, TO LAMBERT

To Lord Father Lambert, by the grace of God bishop of Arras: Walter, provost of the Church of Lille, and his fellow brethren, greetings and devoted service.

Because we believe that the earnestness of your holy request concerning our fellow brother Lord Clarembald has been kindled by the prompting of the Holy Spirit, whom it is not lawful to resist, we feared that not acquiescing in your choice of him—which, with God as author, we trust will result in spiritual benefit—would offend God. Therefore, though grieved because we shall lose in his absence a most excellent example of holy religion, yet labouring for your advancement, in which it is fitting that we rejoice with you, we grant him to serve your fatherhood. Farewell.

### LETTER II. GERWIN, BISHOP OF AMIENS, TO LAMBERT

Gerwin, by the grace of God bishop of Amiens, to Lord Lambert, his dearest brother in Christ, discerning bishop of the holy Church of Arras: may you happily persevere in the purpose of religious life.

In the holy Church of Amiens, which is entrusted to our littleness, a certain shrine has been prepared with great care, labor, and expense by one of our brethren, of gold, silver, and gems, for depositing the relics of the blessed martyr Fuscianus; and by decree of our chapter we have appointed this to be done on the feast of Saint Michael the Archangel. Therefore, by these present letters we earnestly beseech the reverence of your fatherhood, since you are a man who fears God, pleasing both to God and to men in deed and doctrine, with a honey-sweet mouth, that our holy mother Church of Amiens may rejoice in having you as minister and helper for carrying out so great a work. Therefore, that you may have so great a martyr as an intercessor before the tribunal of God, setting aside other business, satisfy this petition of ours and our most ardent desire. [Col. 0648D] Farewell.

## LETTER III. OF RAINOLD, ARCHBISHOP OF RHEIMS, TO LAMBERT

RAINOLD, by the grace of God Archbishop of Rheims, to his beloved brother and fellow-priest LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras, greeting and blessing in the Lord Jesus.

We believe that you retain in memory whatever we recently discussed at length with your fraternity concerning Hugh of Inchy. For this same Hugh very recently came with an armed band to the village of Saint Géry, called Felcherias, during the Truce of God; and, ranging about there on every side, he utterly burned the whole village with fire, and wretchedly carried away with him no small booty and a multitude of people. It has also reached our ears that he boasts of possessing a letter from us by which, whatever madness may have carried him away, he ought—God forbid—to be freed from every fear of the Bishop of Cambrai and from the excommunication of all priests. Therefore, wishing you to know that all his boasting is vain, we command your fraternity both to admonish him, whom we especially love, so that, all excuse removed, you may draw against him the sword of anathema as against a violator of the holy peace; and, until he comes to satisfaction, by the authority of your command you are to forbid the celebration of the divine office in all his residences or in every place where he or his accomplices may be personally present. Farewell.

## LETTER IV. OF THE SAME TO THE SAME

RAINOLD, by the grace of God Archbishop of Rheims, to his brother and fellow-bishop LAMBERT of Arras, greeting and blessing in the Lord Jesus.

For the conference with Count Robert and for receiving justice from him, during the octave of Saint Mary in August, we shall be ready either to present ourselves or to send our messengers, as we have already commanded you and our fellow-bishops of Noyon and Thérouanne. But concerning Hugh of Inchy, about whom you wrote to us, we believe it is clear to you that, at the council which we held at Compiègne in response to the complaints and outcries of Gerard, Bishop of Cambrai, by the judgment of all who were present we drew the sword of anathema against him and against all his helpers and adherents. Yet neither he nor his son ceased to persecute the Church of Cambrai. Indeed, equal expectation of vengeance distressed them, and an equal bond of wickedness and excess bound them together.

Therefore, since, as the Apostle said, “I have become foolish; you compelled me”; and again, in the Acts of the Apostles, to the Jews: “Since you have judged yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles” [Acts 13:46]—so, because this same Hugh judged himself unworthy of conversion and reconciliation, Gerard, Bishop of Cambrai, made an alliance with the Count of Flanders to overcome Hugh’s malice. Consequently, no consideration of equity allowed Gerard, Bishop of Cambrai, to make peace with Hugh without the Count of Flanders; nor indeed did we regard him otherwise than as excommunicated.

But if it depended upon his own will, we should have the Bishop of Cambrai ready at Rheims, at a suitable appointed time, in our presence, both to render and to receive justice from him; and we likewise would weigh the claims of both parties in the equal balance of judgment and mercy, and would not fail to observe moderation in all things. Yet he ought not to come to amendment through you alone, nor to fear only the sentence of your excommunication, since he is known to be a parishioner of the Bishop of Cambrai, and Inchy, through which he exercises this wickedness, lies within the bishopric of Cambrai. Farewell; and write back to us what you have done with the Count of Flanders.

## LETTER V. OF POPPO, BISHOP OF METZ, TO LAMBERT

To Lord LAMBERT, brother and friend, Bishop of Arras, POPPO, by the grace of God Bishop of the city of Metz, the gift of affection and prayer in the Lord.

Having read the letters of your holiness, we render you fitting thanks for the cleric entrusted to us; [Col. 0650B] but I noted why your dignity had refrained from writing in return to our weakness concerning the exchange of fellowship and prayer, when it has been declared by apostolic truth: “Pray for one another, that you may be saved” [James 5:16]. Therefore I urge the eminence of your religious devotion not to refuse to write of your prayers and of the fellowship of those dwelling in the Church of the Mother of God. For these are the things we hoped for from you; these are the means by which we ought happily to commend one another to the eternal King. May your holiness prosper. “May the Dayspring from on high visit us” [Luke 1:78].

## LETTER VI. OF IVO, BISHOP OF CHARTRES, TO LAMBERT

To LAMBERT, by the grace of God Bishop of Arras, IVO, servant of the Church of Chartres, the gift of sincere affection and devoted prayer.

[Col. 0650C] “If the nearness of our places were as great as that of our hearts,” etc., as in Ivo of Chartres, Letter 33.

## LETTER VII. OF WILLIAM, ARCHBISHOP OF ROUEN, TO LAMBERT

WILLIAM, Archbishop of the Church of Rouen, together with the other clergy of the same Church, to LAMBERT, who presides not unfittingly over the Church of Arras, greeting with prayer.

I commend to your fatherhood Richard, ordained priest by me under the mercy of Christ. I pray that under your protection you will not allow him to be subjected to or harassed by any terrors.

## LETTER VIII. OF MANASSES, ARCHDEACON, AND THE CLERGY OF RHEIMS, TO LAMBERT

[Col. 0650D]

To the most reverend lord and father LAMBERT, Bishop of the holy Church of Arras, R. and MANASSES, archdeacons, L., dean, R., cantor, and the whole clergy and people of Rheims, greeting and help from the Lord Jesus.

We considered it fitting to inform your charity that our most reverend father and lord, Archbishop Rainold, entered upon the way of all flesh on the twelfth day before the Kalends of February [21 January], in the triumph of glory. Therefore we earnestly ask your holiness, from the prerogative of due charity, to extend to him the right hand of your prayers and assistance; and, ordering the same to be done in all places over which divine providence has willed you to preside, cause the day of his burial to be entered in remembrance.

Moreover, when our Church, bereft of the defense of so great a father and protector, had begun to suffer grave dangers, and the enemies of God, lying in ambush on every side throughout the land, sought publicly and privately to assail it with countless persecutions, divine mercy, through the spirit of counsel, granted an end to our prayers—mercy which does not permit us to be burdened beyond what we can bear, but with temptation provides an issue, that we may be able to endure [cf. 1 Corinthians 10:13]. Therefore, according to the authority of the holy canons and ecclesiastical custom, by the cooperating grace of the Holy Spirit and the united support of all through petition, we seized for ourselves as archbishop our lord Manasses, provost of our Church, most thoroughly known to us, and irrevocably established him as our lord; for we have greatly rejoiced that he has hitherto burned with most ardent zeal toward us and the whole Church.

Indeed, as he is the most eagerly awaited of all men so far as earthly things are concerned, the longer we delay in seeking him, the more gracious he appears in the eyes of us all. For he is nothing other than a certain perfect perfection gathered from all good things. Hence, as is read of blessed Martin, it happened that we seized him rather than chose him. Let therefore both your kindness and authority, both because of the greatness of his integrity and religious devotion and because of the regard due to our petition, receive and confirm his election with all devotion, and bestow upon him your assistance for such things as must be done, so that through you the Church of Rheims may rejoice in the progress of souls and the completion of good works. Farewell.

The venerable Lord Rainold, Archbishop of Rheims, died in the year of Christ our God 1095, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of February [21 January].

## LETTER IX. OF LAMBERT TO R. AND M., ARCHDEACONS, AND TO THE CLERGY AND PEOPLE OF RHEIMS

To the reverend fathers and lords R. and M., archdeacons, L., dean, R., cantor, and to the whole clergy and people of the holy Church of Rheims, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy Bishop of Arras, their servant and lover of their holiness and salvation, eternal salvation in the Lord.

We wish your love to know that, before we learned from you the day of the death of our venerable father, Lord Archbishop Rainold, we caused the office to be performed both in our own Church and at Saint-Vaast; and we shall urge that it be performed throughout our diocese by congregations both of monks and of clerics. Concerning the election of Lord Manasses, provost of the Church of Rheims, a man to be worthily honored and honorably praised, we rejoice with you, as with our fathers and as with our lords; and rejoicing, we pray God, who is the true joy of all the faithful, that He who began this good work may Himself bring it to completion.

To this election made by you of a person honorable in birth and conduct, as is canonical, we readily give our assent; and we are prepared, in the mercy of God, to provide for you, according to our poverty and your religious devotion, the other things which we owe to the holy Church of Rheims. Most reverend fathers and my lords, fare well in the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete; and do not disdain to pray for me, the servant of your holiness.

Given at Arras, on the fourth day before the Nones of February [2 February].

## LETTER X. OF POPE URBAN II TO THE SUFFRAGANS OF THE CHURCH OF RHEIMS

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his most beloved brethren and fellow-priests, the suffragans of the Church of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0652B] “Upon the death of our venerable fellow-brother,” etc. See Urban II, *Patrology*, vol. 151.

## LETTER XI. OF MANASSES, ELECT OF RHEIMS, TO LAMBERT

MANASSES, by the grace of God elect of Rheims, to LAMBERT, by the same grace Bishop of Arras, greeting and service.

Since my wish and the apostolic command concur, I write to you, my beloved, that, removing every impediment and setting aside every excuse, you should present yourself to the embraces of our affection by Thursday of the first week of Lent. For I ardently desire and earnestly call for advancement to the diaconate and priesthood through the laying on of your hands. Come, however, with few attendants, as the abbot of Saint-Denis informed me that you would do. I say this not to spare my purse, but because I hope that, with a small escort, you will pass more quietly with me through the lands of our enemies on the way to the pope.

Moreover, I share my joy with you: the lord pope and all who are with him rejoice in my election, strengthen it by the authority which they possess, and in no respect withdraw the apostolic arm from me. Farewell.

## LETTER XII. OF POPE URBAN II TO THE CLERGY, KNIGHTS, AND PEOPLE OF RHEIMS

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the clergy, the order, the knights, and the people dwelling at Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0652D] “The inward affections of our love,” etc. See above.

## LETTER XIII. OF POPE URBAN II TO MANASSES

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son MANASSES, elect of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

“We give thanks to almighty God,” etc. See above.

## LETTER XIV. OF URBAN II TO THE SUFFRAGANS OF THE CHURCH OF RHEIMS

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved brethren and fellow-bishops HUGH of Soissons, LAMBERT of Arras, PHILIP of Châlons, GERARD [Col. 0653A] of Thérouanne, and the other suffragans of the Church of Rheims, greeting and apostolic blessing.

“We recently wrote to your fraternity,” etc. See above.

Accordingly, with such strong support of apostolic authority and confirmation, Lord Manasses, the elect, was ordained archbishop at Rheims in the church of Blessed Mary ever Virgin, our Lady. On the Nones of March [7 March], in the first week of Lent at that time, he was ordained deacon by Lord Lambert, Bishop of Arras. Then, on the Saturday of Mid-Lent, he was ordained priest in the aforesaid church of Blessed Mary by Lord Hugh, the venerable Bishop of Soissons. And on the following Sunday, *Judge me, O God* [Psalm 43:1], he was consecrated archbishop at Saint-Remi by the hands of the same Lord Hugh, Bishop of Soissons, while Lord Helinand, Bishop of Laon, Radbod, Bishop of Noyon, Gerewin, Bishop of Amiens, Lambert, Bishop of Arras, and Lietold, Bishop of Senlis, stood by and laid hands upon him. In this order and manner the ordination and consecration of Lord Manasses, Archbishop of Rheims, was completed in the year of Christ our God 1095, on the fourth day before the Kalends of April [29 March].

## LETTER XV. OF POPPO, BISHOP OF METZ, TO LAMBERT

POPPO, by the mercy of God Bishop of Metz, to his beloved father LAMBERT, by the grace of God Bishop of Arras, the duty of affection in all things.

Our most beloved brethren showed us the letters which you sent them; and we granted them whatever you requested, in accordance with their petition and wish. Therefore we humbly ask to share in your prayers, as you wrote to our brethren, so that, watchful through mutual affection for our common salvation, we may at last be able to enjoy eternal blessedness. We also earnestly ask your kindness to commend us personally and intimately to religious men, and to the lord pope; and, wherever need may arise, to support us and our Church in counsel, assistance, and, if necessary, defense, as we trust you will. As for ourselves, be assured that in all things in which we can, we shall make ourselves available to you as need requires, for your worthy honor and advantage. Farewell.

## LETTER XVI. OF ROBERT OF PÉRONNE AND HIS WIFE TO LAMBERT

[Col. 0653D]

To LAMBERT, by the grace of God Bishop of Arras, ROBERT of Péronne and his wife, due affection and submission.

We most humbly beseech your charity that you cause either their goods to be restored to these burgesses of mine who are traveling with wine to Arras, and from whom Arnulf and Radulf of Batpalmes took their wine in the past week after breaking the bond of peace, or that you discharge your office. Farewell.

## LETTER XVII. OF MANASSES OF RHEIMS TO LAMBERT

MANASSES, by the grace of God Archbishop of Rheims, [Col. 0654A] to his brother LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras, abundant salvation and affection in the Lord.

Most beloved brother, we are going to consecrate Lord Manasses, elect of Cambrai, bishop at Rheims during the octave of Pentecost; and we invite the presence of your fraternity to his consecration, declaring to you that it will be most advantageous for the Church of Arras if you attend it. For that complaint which the Church of Cambrai has against the Church of Arras will be greatly weakened if your presence is offered as a cooperating witness at his consecration.

Moreover, we do not wish it to be hidden from your affection that, on the fourth day after the consecration, we and the Count of Flanders, through the mediation of Anselm of Ribemont, shall meet at Cambrai, so that, having expelled that plague from the Church of Cambrai, we may, God favoring us, establish our consecrated bishop in his seat. Therefore let your vigilance approach the count and, with whatever persuasions it can, compel him, in compassion for the Church of Cambrai, to help by expelling that schismatic. Farewell.

## LETTER XVIII. OF LAMBERT TO EVRARD, ADVOCATE OF TOURNAI

To his beloved lord, friend, and parishioner EVRARD, advocate of Tournai, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy Bishop of Arras, eternal salvation in the Lord.

If you knew how great and what kind of punishment awaits those who, contrary to the decrees of the holy Fathers and canons, usurp tithes and altar offerings which are due to clerics alone, you would never presume to usurp the altar of Saint Mary of the Castle. Therefore remember the destruction of the sons of Korah, who, usurping what was due to the priests, were swallowed alive when the earth engulfed them. King Saul likewise, because he usurped for himself the office of sacrifice, being condemned by God lost both kingdom and life. King Uzziah also, for a like reason, was struck by God with leprosy.

Therefore, just as it is not your place, nor that of any layman in the Church of God, to preach, baptize, receive confessions, impose penances, or sacrifice, so it belongs to none of you to claim tithes and altar offerings for himself. Accordingly, we command your affection both to restore the aforesaid altar to us in peace and to allow us to retain it. But if you are unwilling to do this, we shall forbid the divine office to be performed there, as has been established in councils. Farewell, and do what belongs to God.

## LETTER XIX. OF MANASSES OF RHEIMS TO THE CLERICS AND ALELMUS OF PASSO

MANASSES, by the grace of God Archbishop of Rheims, to the clerics and to ALELMUS OF PASSO: conversion from error.

Because, despising the apostolic decree, you refused to obey our most beloved fellow-brother and fellow-bishop Lambert of Arras, we pursue and confirm by metropolitan authority the excommunication pronounced upon you by him and strengthened by apostolic authority. Therefore we command you, within eight days after you have seen these letters, to present yourselves before the aforesaid fellow-brother [Col. 0655A] of ours in order to make fitting satisfaction for your so bold rebellion; and thereafter to obey him altogether as your father and bishop.

## LETTER XX. OF MANASSES TO THE CLERGY, LEADING MEN, AND PEOPLE OF CAMBRAI

MANASSES, by the grace of God Archbishop of Rheims, to all abbots, archdeacons, deans, and the whole clergy of Cambrai; to Count B., Count G., A. T. of Avesnes, with the other leading men; and to the whole people of the Church of Cambrai, greeting.

We believe that for many days now you have beheld the misery and affliction of the Church of Cambrai, which the devil of all wicked men has inflicted and continues to inflict through that accursed Gualcherius, to whom a great host of his retinue lends support. We also believe that you yield to the tears of that Church and sympathize with them as men of mercy, as sons of obedience, as those who, being Christ’s, have no compact with Belial. We received at Rheims, in the charity which we owed them, the children of that Church, who, because of obedience to the lord pope and because they kept the commands of ourselves and of their mother Church of Rheims, had been driven by that accursed man from their own seats in all want and nakedness. We fixed for them a day on which we would consecrate their elect, Lord Manasses; and immediately after the consecration we would bring him to you and place him in your hands as the shepherd of your souls.

But because the course of this affair made the presence of our beloved son, the Count of Flanders, absolutely necessary, and because it was not lawful to confer with him about these matters beforehand while he was absent, the consecration of the elect of Cambrai, which we had set, was delayed for a short time. Yet, that meanwhile we might heal the desolation of our children of Cambrai, at their request and by the judgment of our fellow-bishops we resorted to these remedies. By apostolic authority and our own, we entrusted to the Bishop of Arras, though he resisted, the power of binding and loosing and the administration of every episcopal office in the bishopric of Cambrai; and we send him back to you under the privilege of this authority, bearing upon his shoulders—the shoulders of mercy—the scattered flock entrusted to him.

Therefore, most beloved, I summon you in the spirit of mercy and compassion, and, commanding, adjure you by apostolic authority and our own: render every obedience to the bishop to whom we have committed it; and cause the clergy of Cambrai, driven from their seats because they have kept the commandments of God, to possess in complete security and peace whatever property of the bishopric of Cambrai and of the community of brethren, and of those schismatics who still remain at Cambrai with that member of Satan, is situated anywhere in your counties or within your power. And this I command you for the remission of your sins. Remember, sons, that you bear the sword for this cause. Consider, most beloved, that this is the way to that Jerusalem which is heavenly. “Come, children, hear me; I will teach you the fear of God” [Psalm 34:11]. Farewell.

## LETTER XXI. OF HUGH, BISHOP OF LYONS, TO LAMBERT

HUGH, servant of the holy Church of Lyons, to his most reverend brother LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras, greeting.

We take care to make known to your affection our sister in Christ, Emma, etc. See Hugh of Lyons, *Patrology*, vol. 157.

## LETTER XXII. OF HUGH OF SOISSONS TO LAMBERT

To LAMBERT, by the grace of God Bishop of Arras, HUGH, Bishop of Soissons, greeting and affection in Christ.

[Col. 0656B] I send to your fraternity this parishioner of ours, named Herimar, that you may cause to be restored to him the money for four cartloads of wine which Gormar and his son Reiner owe and unjustly withhold. We have heard that he wishes to go to Jerusalem. But let the prudence of your fatherhood forbid him to carry this money with him. For alms must not be made from plunder. You also know that this has been forbidden by the lord pope: that no one should carry another person’s property on this journey. Therefore I ask your affection that, unless they restore the debt, you administer against them, for my sake, the justice which pertains to you. Farewell.

## LETTER XXIII. OF RADBOD OF TOURNAI TO LAMBERT

[Col. 0656C]

To LAMBERT, by the grace of God venerable Bishop of Arras, RADBOD, humble bishop of the people of Tournai, greeting and affection in the Lord.

The ancient enemy of the human race, inflamed by the torches of envy, strives with every effort to disturb the peace of the Church, which he understands to be harmful to his deceits. But those—I mean the bishops—to whom the staff for defending the Christian fold has been entrusted ought to repel attacking wolves from injuring the Lord’s sheep. Nor is it right only that we guard and bestow care upon those especially entrusted to us; we must also, from affection of charity and zeal of compassion, watch over those belonging to others.

Let, therefore, the pitiable complaint of the monks of Saint-Amand and the detestable wrong most unjustly inflicted upon them by our subjects move your compassion. For recently, when I was passing through their place, they complained to me—not without deep contrition of spirit, abundant shedding of tears, and groaning drawn from their inmost depths, which interrupted their speech—of violent plundering of their lands, most savage beatings of men, punitive imprisonment, and intolerable ransoms exacted to the last farthing. They mournfully lament that all these things are inflicted upon them by Anselm and his seneschal Rainer.

Hearing this of the perversity of your parishioner, I grieve; grieving, I protest; protesting, I humbly implore your counsel and assistance: namely, that you compel him to make satisfaction by your own excommunication, and grant me permission to excommunicate him. Unless he comes to satisfaction, the monks, laying the holy relics upon the ground, will invoke God for vengeance in this matter and will anathematize Anselm and his supporters with curses and execrations. Farewell.

## LETTER XXIV. OF MANASSES OF CAMBRAI TO LAMBERT

To LAMBERT, by the grace of God Bishop of Arras, MANASSES, by the same grace Bishop of the people of Cambrai, greeting and mutual affection in Christ.

I pray for your love and brotherhood, that you send me by the present messenger the blessing of churches and reconciliation. For on the coming Sunday, God’s mercy granting it, I have resolved to consecrate a church; and, as a friend from a friend, I have not doubted to seek from you those things necessary to our office. Farewell.

## LETTER XXV. OF LAMBERT TO THE BRETHREN OF THE MONASTERY OF WATTEN

LAMBERT, by God’s mercy Bishop of Arras, to Lord BERNOLD, provost, RICHOARD, dean, and the other brethren of the monastery of Watten: to do all things honorably and in due order.

Since it is clear from the authorities of the holy canons that a cleric may not go into another bishop’s diocese without letters of commendation from his own bishop, nor ought he to be received there, we greatly wonder at your prudence, which should preserve rather than transgress the canons—the treasure of our Church—yet has so suddenly and unlawfully seized Lord Achard, our son and provost of Saint Mary. Therefore, considering that our father Pope Damasus has pronounced against such violators a judgment whose authority is not unknown to you, take care to return honorably and properly, by the Sunday *Populus Sion*, our beloved brother whom you received improperly and dishonorably against right and without reasonable cause, and whom, though there was no necessity that he should become a canon, you made a canon.

Moreover, we summon Brother Achard before you as a canon, that by the same deadline he may come to make satisfaction for so grave a fault. But if not, established upon the authorities of Scripture and the counsel of our metropolitan and fellow-bishops, we shall draw against him the sword of the sentence which is fitting; and thereafter we shall regard you as disobedient to the Holy Spirit, whom it is sinful to oppose.

## LETTER XXVI. OF GERARD, BISHOP OF THE MORINI, TO LAMBERT

To the lord and venerable LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras, GERARD, Bishop of the Morini, greeting in the Lord Jesus.

We send to your holiness this cleric named Tainbold, that you may advance him to the order of priesthood. Farewell.

## LETTER XXVII. OF HUGH, BISHOP OF SOISSONS, AND ANSELM, ELECT OF BEAUVAIS, TO LAMBERT

To LAMBERT, by the grace of God Bishop of Arras, HUGH, [Col. 0658A] by the grace of God Bishop of Soissons, and ANSELM, elect of Beauvais, greeting in the Lord Jesus.

Discussing our affairs in confidence, as kinsmen and friends, we earnestly request that you direct the sum of our counsels and actions to an honorable conclusion, since we have found you endowed with outstanding wisdom in many and great deliberations. And because we wish to speak with you confidentially and cannot adequately set forth everything in letters, we ask your kindness to meet us in the town called Montmirel, situated in your diocese and considered close to your city. Be with us at first light on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of January [17 December]. Farewell.

## LETTER XXVIII. OF GEREWIN OF AMIENS TO LAMBERT

GEREWIN, by the grace of God Bishop of the people of Amiens, to the venerable LAMBERT, bishop of the people of Arras: to glory eternally with Christ.

At the request of Lord Hugh, Abbot of Cluny, whom all the faithful ought to obey, we command your fraternity to confer, in our stead, upon these four monks and one cleric the orders which they request. For at present, certain causes preventing it, I have not resolved to confer orders. Farewell.

## LETTER XXIX. OF LAMBERT TO GERARD, BISHOP OF THÉROUANNE

To the honorable lord GERARD, by the grace of God Bishop of Thérouanne, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy Bishop of Arras, eternal salvation in the Lord.

[Col. 0658C] When we approached the authority of your reverence during Advent, we complained concerning Lord Achard, our provost and canon, that, departing from us in disobedience, he is being held in your bishopric contrary to canon law. We earnestly requested that he be restored to us and that he not be ordained by anyone with your permission, as authority requires; but your prudence did not heed us when we cried out. Now, however, through these present letters, we are compelled by brotherly piety to appeal to your mercy, asking that you command our sheep, which strayed from the flock in disobedience, to be returned by your authority by the Conversion of Saint Paul [25 January]. Otherwise, know that we shall bring a complaint concerning this matter before our masters and, God helping us, obtain justice.

We must not neglect, as we have professed, to observe what Pope Leo the Great and Doctor decreed concerning clerics of this kind, disobedient to their bishops and transferring to other Churches. For he says: “Let no one receive or solicit another bishop’s cleric against his bishop’s will, unless perhaps this is agreed between the giver and receiver by an arrangement of charity. For he is guilty of grave injury who dares either to cast away or retain from the Church of his brother that which is more useful or precious. Therefore, if the matter is conducted within a province, the metropolitan shall compel the fugitive cleric to return to his own Church.”

Likewise, concerning the same matter, in the Council of Carthage, chapter 20: no one may dare either to retain or advance in the Church entrusted to him a cleric belonging to another, unless the cleric’s own bishop grants permission. Likewise, from the authority of the same council, chapter 15, we must observe that laymen who despise the canons are to be excommunicated, while clerics are to be deprived of rank. Since, therefore, the authority of the saints excommunicates laymen who despise the canons and deprives clerics of rank, we wonder that you have not yet done what is brotherly and episcopal toward us and toward our Church, your mother. Fare well.

## LETTER XXX. OF HUGH OF SOISSONS TO LAMBERT

To his most beloved fellow-brother—indeed, father—LAMBERT, venerable Bishop of Arras, HUGH, by the grace of God Bishop of Soissons, greeting and glory in the Lord.

I lament before your affection that I have again been wronged and more shamefully despised by that rebellious and sacrilegious man of Saint-Médard—not an abbot but an intruder—after the first injury. For he scorned the manner of making satisfaction to me which was confirmed at Rheims by the decree of you and the other fellow-bishops. Therefore I ask your greatest and dearest brotherhood, in accordance with what you decreed together should be done to the disobedient and perverse man, to excommunicate that thief and robber, who is unrepentant and excommunicated by me. For you likewise promised me your aid for this very purpose. Farewell. Therefore I ask that you do this on the approaching day of the Lord’s Supper.

## LETTER XXXI. OF LAMBERT TO CLEMENTIA, COUNTESS OF FLANDERS

LAMBERT, by God’s mercy Bishop of Arras, to his honorable lady CLEMENTIA, [Col. 0659C] Countess of Flanders, greeting and service with prayers.

We wish to make known to your nobility that certain pilgrims, our parishioners, coming from Rome, passed peacefully through all foreign lands. At last, upon reaching your land, they were plundered by your provost G. at Batpalmes. Desiring to carry out the ministry which pertains to us, we commanded him either freely or under surety to restore what he had unjustly taken in time of peace. When he refused to do this, we excommunicated him on Maundy Thursday. Now we ask your mercy to deal with such a man according to the peace and cause the pilgrims’ property to be restored to them. But if it is not restored, since we cannot alter the statutes of peace, we shall place under ban the entire castle in which this crime and many other crimes were committed. Farewell.

## LETTER XXXII. OF HUGH OF SOISSONS TO LAMBERT

To his reverend and beloved lord LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras, HUGH, by the grace of God Bishop of Soissons, greeting and service in Christ.

I have frequently and abundantly experienced that your affection is sufficiently well disposed toward us and greatly helpful. But in the matter most particularly pursued concerning the abbot of Saint-Médard, the deed itself, settled by your counsel and assistance, shows how you have been my helper. For I wish you to know that this abbot came to us humbly, confessing that he had sinned. When he asked to be absolved, we absolved him; and, when the former abbot of that monastery had resigned into our hands its care and pastoral staff, and an election concerning Radulf himself had been presented to us, we made him abbot.

But before these matters were completed, the king, in letters sent to me, showed that he took this dispute badly, adjured me, and summoned me both to a conference and to prayer. Wishing to avoid his hostility, we thus accomplished those things with the fullness of our jurisdiction confirmed. Therefore I ask that you absolve him, now amended and absolved. Farewell.

## LETTER XXXIII. OF MANASSES OF RHEIMS TO LAMBERT

MANASSES, by the grace of God Archbishop of Rheims, to LAMBERT, by the same grace Bishop of the Church of Arras, greeting and a state of complete felicity.

[Col. 0660B] Let your affection know, most beloved brother in Christ, that Lord Ingelram, bishop of the Church of Laon, has returned from the archbishop of Lyons with the authorization and assent to ordain and consecrate as bishop Lord Anselm, elect of the Church of Beauvais. Therefore, lest the Church of Beauvais be deprived any longer of the administration of episcopal offices, we admonish you by the authority with which we preside not to withhold, through any neglect, from the aforesaid elect that which belongs to your office; but, setting far aside every pretext that might hinder, remember to attend his consecration at Rheims on the Sunday immediately following the octave of Pentecost. Farewell.

## LETTER XXXIV. FROM LAMBERT TO POPE URBAN.

[Col. 0660C]

To the most reverend lord and Father of fathers, Pope URBAN, LAMBERT, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Arras, due submission with prayers.

We wish Your Holiness to know that we, the abbots of our province, and our fellow bishops were summoned to Rheims by our metropolitan concerning certain ecclesiastical affairs. There, among other matters, Lord B., abbot of Marmoutier, laid claim to the person of his brother and son Robert, abbot of the monastery of Saint-Remi, affirming on his word of truth that neither personally nor through anyone sent by him had he ever released Robert entirely to the Church of Rheims, except with preservation of his profession and subjection to Marmoutier; and the lord archbishop of Rheims declared that this was indeed so.

The abbot further stated that, having heard that many disorderly and irregular things were being done by the aforesaid Abbot Robert, he first admonished him by letter, and afterwards through suitable persons under obedience, to present himself before the abbot in the chapter-house of Marmoutier on a day and at a time appointed for him, to answer concerning his life and conduct; otherwise, the abbot was to pronounce sentence upon him as one guilty of violating his profession and of despising the holy Rule. Brother R., the abbot, having reported this to the lord archbishop, received from him counsel and command that he should in no manner or on any pretext set himself against his father, namely the abbot of Marmoutier; [Col. 0661A] and that, if he presumed to do so, whatever sentence the aforesaid abbot should pronounce against him, the lord archbishop would approve and confirm.

But when, at the prescribed term, he did not present himself at Marmoutier as had been ordered, the abbot of Marmoutier pronounced against him a sentence of excommunication. Having been admonished of all these matters by our archbishop, and since Robert was unable by canonical argument to oppose the words of his abbot, it was judged by the bishops and abbots that one monk was not to be retained by the archbishop away from another, but was to be restored entirely to the authority of his own abbot. On hearing this, however, he turned away from the judgment of justice and summoned us, our fellow bishops, and the abbots before the apostolic tribunal, in order to evade discipline.

For this reason we have set forth the course of the matter for your justice: if this disobedient and excommunicated man should come to you, do not hear him against the judgment of the bishops and against the religious order of the abbots. Rather, we humbly entreat, prostrate at the feet of Your Holiness, that their sentence may obtain strength through your authority. Fare well, most reverend lord and Father; and do not disdain to pray for us, who by your obedience are placed in the greatest danger and distress.

## LETTER XXXV. FROM MANASSES OF RHEIMS TO LAMBERT.

MANASSES, by the grace of God archbishop of Rheims, to LAMBERT, by the same grace bishop of the Church of Arras, greetings and love in the Lord.

The community of the Church of Thérouanne and Bernold, abbot [Col. 0661C] of Watten, together with the flock entrusted to him, earnestly desiring in pious devotion the consecration of the church of Watten, and observing that at this time authority to perform this office has not been granted to Lord Gerard, bishop of Thérouanne, requested of us—upon whose care the pastoral charge now depends—that we entrust the office of this consecration to one of our fellow bishops. But we, fearing that some impediment on the journey may befall bishops who are farther away, and considering the various misdeeds of various persons, enjoin upon you the office of this consecration, because you are nearer than the others, because, as we hope, you can travel there without hindrance, and because you are familiar with that church. [Col. 0661D] We command you, supported by our authority, to establish forever the liberty of the aforesaid church according to the decrees and ordinances of the canons. Farewell.

## LETTER XXXVI. FROM LAMBERT TO POPE URBAN.

To the most reverend lord and Father of fathers, Pope URBAN, LAMBERT, bishop of the holy Church of Arras, an unprofitable servant, due obedience with prayers.

Lord Gerard, bishop of Thérouanne, hoping that we might intercede for him with Your Holiness, asked us to send our letter to you on his behalf. But, being unaware what you determined concerning his case after the Council of Nîmes, we entreat Your Holiness, as we did then and still do now, at his request, that you may show him mercy according to God. [Col. 0662A] Fare well, most reverend lord.

## LETTER XXXVII. FROM ANSELM OF CANTERBURY TO LAMBERT.

ANSELM, archbishop of Canterbury, to his friend the reverend bishop LAMBERT of Arras, greetings.

I ask Your Holiness, for love of the lord pope and of myself, to have this clerk of his escorted through your bishopric as far as seems good to you. Farewell.

## LETTER XXXVIII. FROM HUGH, BISHOP OF LYONS, TO LAMBERT.

To the venerable brother LAMBERT, bishop of Arras, HUGH, servant of the Church of Lyons, greetings.

“This brother, the bearer [of this letter], etc.” See Hugh of Lyons, [Col. 0662B] *Patrologia*, vol. CLVII.

## LETTER XXXIX. FROM LAMBERT TO CLEMENCE, COUNTESS OF FLANDERS.

LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras, to his honourable lady CLEMENCE, countess of the Flemings, greetings and faithful service with prayers.

Lord Manasses, archbishop of Rheims, recently sent me letters concerning the Church of Thérouanne, instructing me to call you to account, either personally or by our letters, concerning Robert and his fortification, through which he does not cease to plunder and devastate the aforesaid church and the property of its clergy; and to let him know on the next Sunday, when *Populus Sion* is sung, what answer you give. We therefore ask Your Excellency and counsel your honour to answer the archbishop so justly and honourably that he may find in you neither fault nor injustice on Robert’s behalf against the Church of Thérouanne, your mother. Fare well always in the Lord. Amen.

## LETTER XL. FROM LAMBERT TO GONFRID, CASTELLAN OF LENS.

LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras, to his honourable lord and friend GONFRID, castellan of Lens—though he deserves otherwise—greetings and love with prayers.

A grave complaint concerning you has reached our synod: that you have violated the churchyard of Lothes and the land belonging to the church of that [Col. 0662D] churchyard, and that, without consulting us, you have retained for yourself, solely at your own will, the property of its people—even though, as is said, they were liable to your jurisdiction. This neither you nor any earthly power is permitted to do: it is contrary to the liberty of the holy Church of God, your mother; contrary to the excommunication protecting churchyards and sanctuary lands; and contrary to the sworn peace.

We therefore greatly wonder that you have committed so grave an evil in our region—something you are not accustomed to do—when it is well established that in the land of your birth you have always been law-abiding and very moderate. We wish you to know that Uzziah, king of Israel, was struck by the Lord with perpetual leprosy because he presumed to usurp the office of the priesthood. Likewise Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, because he did not give glory [Col. 0663A] to God, received from God, the Creator of all, a harsh punishment outside human society for seven years.

Therefore, since these things, and whatever things have been written, were written for our instruction, according to the Apostle Paul, by these letters we summon you into our presence for the correction and salvation of your soul, together with those who were your accomplices in this perverse deed. We have for this reason deferred pronouncing upon you the synodal sentence of excommunication: because we desire more earnestly that you and the evil-doers involved in this action should be humbly saved than stubbornly and proudly condemned. If, therefore, within fifteen days from today, after seeing our letters, you should refuse—which God forbid—to make satisfaction to God and to us in accordance with the ordinance concerning the liberty and peace of churchyards and sanctuary lands, then, with the help of the Saviour of all, and as the severity of the holy canons directs, we shall not delay to pronounce excommunication [Col. 0663B] upon those whom we have already summoned and banned, and upon their defenders. Farewell.

## LETTER XLI. FROM MANASSES OF RHEIMS TO LAMBERT.

MANASSES, by the grace of God archbishop of Rheims, to his beloved fellow brother and fellow priest LAMBERT, by the same grace bishop of Arras, greetings and an abundance of love.

The Church of Noyon, grieving that it is deprived of the comfort and due care of its pastor, and tearfully revealing to us the persecution which it suffers inwardly and outwardly, presented to us the election of Lord Baldric, made with the great and unanimous consent [Col. 0663C] of clergy and people. Since we found nothing in it contrary to the sacred canons, we approved it with our assent and fixed the Sunday in the octave of this approaching Pentecost as the day of his consecration. We admonish and invite your affection to it, so that you may fulfill in the elect what belongs to your office; setting far aside every pretext that might hinder, remember to be at Rheims on the aforesaid day.

Yet, in order that you may relieve us of some portion of our labour, we wish you to come on Thursday or Friday, so that you may ordain candidates on our behalf on Saturday. Farewell.

## LETTER XLII. FROM R., DEAN OF NOYON, TO LAMBERT.

To the most reverend and most beloved lord LAMBERT, [Col. 0663D] bishop of Arras, R., dean of the Church of Noyon, and the congregation subject to him, faithful prayers and the fullest love in the Lord.

Let your fatherhood know, lord, that our church, bereft of the comfort of our deceased pastor, battered at once by many shipwrecks and oppressed also by many storms of persecution, has scarcely been brought back to the harbour of saving consolation. But because God’s merciful providence does not despise the groans of those who hope in him, he has deigned to visit the misery of his people and, through the election of a pastor, to restore his Church to the privilege of its lost joy.

For it has, by the common counsel and assent of clergy and people, a pastor not brought in from elsewhere, not another man, but its own: one whom it brought forth from its own [Col. 0664A] womb, received in its bosom, and itself nursed; whom it itself reared after weaning; and whom, from the very beginning of his cradle, through the stages of ages and orders, it wholly claimed as its own. Thus it rejoices to have, from a son, a father; from one it has nourished, a ruler; from its own canon and archdeacon, Baldric, a bishop. For we know no one in the whole Church more worthy of this promotion.

Therefore, most holy Father, since you love our consolation, as we believe, with brotherly goodwill, we ask you to convey your assent in this matter to our lord archbishop and, in consecrating the pastor, to show us the charitable comfort and assistance of your presence. Farewell.

## LETTER XLIII. FROM LAMBERT TO MANASSES OF RHEIMS.

[Col. 0664B] To the honourable lord and dearest Father MANASSES, by the grace of God archbishop of Rheims, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras, eternal salvation in the Lord.

Your fatherhood invited us much too late to the consecration of the elect of Noyon, particularly since neither an abundance of resources nor safety of roads is available to us. Moreover, remember that whenever you commanded and we were able, without excuse we have served you and our mother, the Church of Rheims, not merely once but often, and are ready to serve. But because at present we are hindered by the matters mentioned above and others which we shall later submit to your fatherhood, we ask that Your Highness not be angry with us.

Whatever your metropolitan authority shall decree to be done that is not contrary to the sacred canons or to the commands of the Apostolic See, [Col. 0664C] we gladly approve and, in approving, confirm. Farewell.

## LETTER XLIV. FROM GUY, COUNT OF PONTHIEU, TO LAMBERT.

To LAMBERT, by the grace of God bishop of Arras and his kinsman, GUY, count of Ponthieu, greetings and friendship.

I humbly entreat your goodness to deign to come to Abbeville on the seventh day of Pentecost, because on the following Sunday I am to equip and honour Louis, the king’s son, with the arms of knighthood, and advance and admit him to knighthood. I therefore ask you to come in order to honour Louis himself. I desired the authority of your counsel to be present in this undertaking. [Col. 0664D] Thus, even if you decline to come for Louis himself, I nevertheless beg you to deign to come for my sake and for the kinship existing between you and me; and, in return for whatever favour you may henceforth be able to obtain from me, I ask you to come on the Saturday of Pentecost. Farewell.

## LETTER XLV. FROM CLEMENCE, COUNTESS OF FLANDERS, TO LAMBERT.

CLEMENCE, by God’s will countess of Flanders, to LAMBERT, her most beloved bishop of Arras, every blessing desired in the Lord.

Because the case being discussed between me and the clerics of the Church of Thérouanne is known to you, I judged it superfluous to report it to you again. Yet because I have no small confidence in you, I command you and admonish you as a friend to send a messenger or letters to the archbishop with mine; urge and persuade him to do full justice concerning those who wrong me, and not delay to give counsel suited to me and to my honour in this matter, lest, if his justice fails, I must extend my hand in revenge. Farewell.

## LETTER XLVI. FROM POPPO, BISHOP OF METZ, TO LAMBERT.

To LAMBERT, bishop of the holy Church of Arras, most worthy of every reverence, POPPO, fellow brother and fellow bishop of Metz, perseverance in good works.

Since we have learned from the sons of our Church that you entered into a great bond of friendship, in some fashion, with our lord predecessor Herman, in whose office we, though unworthy, serve in his place, and since the opportunity of our own affairs has so presented itself, we would earnestly desire that this same pact of friendship be renewed between us all the more greatly because we see ourselves to be more in need of assistance. [Col. 0665B] For through the joy of this union we believe great comfort would come to us, since fellowship with good persons greatly benefits the weakness of those less strong, as the authority of Holy Scripture confirms.

And if you should ever decide, in return for the bond with that same Lord Herman, to visit the place in which his buried limbs rest, your presence would bring us no small gladness of heart. Since, because of the exile of persecution, suitable places are lacking for carrying out the duties of ordination, moved by the prayers of these our sons, we have decided to send them to your affection so that they may shortly be advanced by you through the grades of consecration. Farewell.

## LETTER XLVII. FROM PHILIP, BISHOP OF CHÂLONS, TO LAMBERT.

To LAMBERT, most reverend bishop of the Church of Arras, PHILIP, bishop of Châlons: “May you be clothed with the stole of immortality.”

Since it is indeed our duty to assist all the children of the holy Church in their necessities, we must take especial care to render the help of consolation to those who, out of fear for the heavenly homeland, we believe have forsaken the comfort of this world. Therefore, venerable Father, we entreat your charity [Col. 0665D] to advance to holy orders, within our bishopric—that is, in the Church of All Saints—these brothers whom the venerable Poppo, bishop of Metz, has sent to us for consecration. For I, entangled in secular cares, am at present unable to perform this kind of office. Farewell.

## LETTER LXVIII. FROM POPE URBAN II TO MANASSES OF RHEIMS.

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the most reverend brother and fellow bishop MANASSES, archbishop of Rheims, greetings and the apostolic blessing.

“Although [we have received] the letter of the clerics of Noyon, etc.” See Pope Urban II, *Patrologia*, vol. CLI.

## LETTER XLIX. FROM MANASSES OF RHEIMS TO LAMBERT.

[Col. 0666A]

MANASSES, by the grace of God archbishop of Rheims, to his beloved brother and fellow bishop Lambert of Arras, greetings and every joy.

We wish you to know, most beloved brother in Christ, that the lord pope has sent the elect of Noyon, Lord Baldric, back to us with his letters, that we may render him what is due to him; and that, with the counsel of our Church, we have fixed the day of his consecration for the Sunday immediately after Epiphany. We therefore invite your brotherhood by this present letter to his consecration, setting aside every excuse, that on the aforesaid day you may render him his due together with us. Farewell.

## LETTER L. FROM THE SAME TO THE CLERGY AND PEOPLE OF THÉROUANNE.

[Col. 0666B]

MANASSES, by the grace of God archbishop of Rheims, to the clergy, order, and people of Thérouanne, greetings and love.

Let your affection know, dearly beloved, that among the other commands which the lord pope sent to us through our bishops who have returned from Rome, he especially commanded us to provide for your Church, lest it remain longer deprived of the consolation of a pastor, but may obtain one without delay. Therefore, by the authority with which we preside over you as sons, we command you to present on the coming Friday Lord John—whose election the lord pope and the Roman council approve and confirm—to the bishop of Arras. [Col. 0666C] We command that bishop, in our stead, to advance John to the priesthood, not wishing to burden him by bringing him with you all the way to us, so that we in turn may as soon as possible lay the hand of consecration upon him.

But if you plead excuses, if you prefer to introduce delays, the Lord will have the blood of his people to demand from your hands. Farewell.

## LETTER LI. FROM THE CLERGY AND PEOPLE OF THÉROUANNE TO LAMBERT.

To their lord LAMBERT, by the grace of God bishop of Arras, all the clergy and people of Thérouanne: cooperation of the Holy Spirit in good works.

Having received the lord pope’s letters concerning confirmation of the election of Lord John, archdeacon of Arras, we unanimously approve it in heart and mind, knowing him to be a man of good reputation and, in life and conduct, suitable for so great an office. [Col. 0666D] And since our Church can no longer remain without episcopal offices, we beseech Your Holiness, because of the danger which, as you know, daily threatens that church, to hasten through advancing our elect to the priesthood to come to its aid by your charity, so that, thereafter, without any delay, he may receive episcopal consecration by the Lord’s favour.

May the grace of the Lord grant that he may keep watch so over the flock to be entrusted to him that he deserves to hear from Him: “Well done, good servant.” Farewell.

## LETTER LII. FROM MANASSES OF CAMBRAI TO LAMBERT.

To his lord and fellow brother LAMBERT, by the grace of God [Col. 0667A] bishop of Arras, MANASSES, bishop of the Church of Cambrai by the same grace, greetings and service.

We inform Your Holiness that the church of Fécamp, because it lacks its own pastor, is very desolate. For its consolation the brethren of that monastery have elected as abbot a monk of Anchin named Taimbald, and they asked us to appeal to your fatherhood about this. We, acceding by the duty of paternal charity to their prayers, command you and beseech you in a spirit of humility to deign, in so great a necessity, to urge the monk to accept the office of abbot; and, if it is just and canonical, even to compel him by obedience. Farewell.

## LETTER LIII. FROM IDA, COUNTESS OF HAINAUT, TO LAMBERT.

[Col. 0667B]

To LAMBERT, by the grace of God bishop of Arras, IDA, countess of Hainaut, greetings and obedience.

Most sweet father, I confidently appeal to your fatherhood that, just as in other matters I have found you a useful friend, so in this affair I may find you an advocate against an unjust accusation, lest I or my land be deliberately struck by a sentence of excommunication. I am ready to make satisfaction before you in all things. Farewell.

## LETTER LIV. FROM PHILIP OF CHÂLONS TO LAMBERT.

To his dearest lord and friend LAMBERT, venerable bishop of Arras by God’s grace, PHILIP, by the same grace bishop of Châlons, faithful service with prayers.

[Col. 0667C] Since, with divine help, we are to dedicate the church of Blessed Memmius, our first pastor, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of November, we invite your brotherhood to this celebration. We wish you to be present at so great a solemnity, both because of the excellence of holiness in which you surpass others and because we desire to revive our former affection through mutual conversation. Blessed Memmius therefore asks you, and we too ask you, by the love we trust you bear toward us, that your highness may visit our lowliness and not disdain to attend the consecration of the aforesaid church. Farewell.

## LETTER LV. FROM R[OBERT], ABBOT OF SAINT-REMI, TO LAMBERT.

To his lord LAMBERT, bishop of Arras by God’s grace, Brother R., expelled abbot of Saint-Remi, what a son owes to a father and a servant to a lord.

We wish to send Your Fatherhood the letters concerning our judgment rendered at Rome, so that it may be known to you that I have never been deposed by any judgment. We likewise wish your affection to know what words the pope uttered against Ulric when he accused me, saying only that the abbot of Marmoutier had not entirely released me from the yoke of his lordship. I call God to witness that I shall speak truthfully, according to my understanding, and have committed it to writing with the testimony of those who were present with me. [Col. 0668A] Even if I do not give the identical syllables and exact wording, I shall nevertheless give words equivalent in force and in the arrangement of the statement.

He said, therefore: “In the entire sequence of the holy canons we have never found an archabbot mentioned. It would certainly have been mentioned if one abbot ought to be set over another. But just as no one can serve two masters, so no one can obey two professions. For, once a monk has been sent forth from his own church and promoted to be an abbot, he is monk of the church of which he is abbot.” He said these things. You, therefore, consider how rightly our archbishop acted against me, and we ask you to be our intercessor with him.

## LETTER LVI. FROM MANASSES OF RHEIMS TO LAMBERT.

[Col. 0668B] MANASSES, by the grace of God archbishop of Rheims, to LAMBERT, his fellow brother, bishop of Arras, greetings in Christ Jesus.

Let it be known to you, dearest brother, that a true and joyful report has newly reached our ears—a report which we believe descended not from human power but indeed from the divine Majesty: namely, that Jerusalem stands on high in joy and gladness, Jerusalem, the city of our redemption and glory, rejoices with unlooked-for joy because, through the incomparable labour and power of the sons of God, it has been delivered from the most cruel bondage of the pagans. Let us also rejoice, whose Christian faith has in these times been placed in the mirror of eternal brightness.

[Col. 0668C] Therefore, admonished, summoned, and compelled not only by the letters of Lord Pope Paschal, but also by the most humble entreaties of Duke Godfrey, whom the army of Christ by divine appointment raised to be king, and likewise by the honeyed supplications of Lord Arnulf, whom it unanimously elected to the patriarchate of the see of Jerusalem, we command you with like charity that you cause unceasing prayers to be offered in every church of your parishes, with fasting and almsgiving: that the King of kings and Lord of lords may grant the king victory over the enemies of Christians, and may grant the patriarch religious steadfastness and wisdom against the sects and deceits of heretics.

We likewise command and admonish you under obedience to compel by threats all who, having taken a vow, have made upon themselves the sign of the cross [Col. 0668D] in order to set out for Jerusalem to assist their brothers, provided they are sound in body and possess the means to complete the journey. Moreover, do not cease diligently and most devoutly to exhort others by your preaching not to neglect aiding the people of God, so that, just as the first, so also the last may together receive the denarius promised to labourers in the vineyard. Farewell.

Pray for the bishop of Le Puy, [Note: [Col. 0667D] Adhémar de Monteil, bishop of Le Puy, had followed the army of the crusaders as papal legate; he died at Antioch after the capture of that city. It is claimed that in memory of this prelate the bishops of Le Puy placed a sword [Col. 0668D] in their arms, and that the canons wore a piece of fur shaped like a cuirass, called a *lingarelle*.—*Acts of the Province of Rheims*, II, 146, note.] for the bishop of Orange, for Anselm of Ribemont, [Col. 0669A] and for all the others who, crowned with so glorious a martyrdom, have died in peace.

## LETTER LVII. FROM MANASSES OF RHEIMS TO LAMBERT.

MANASSES, by the grace of God archbishop of Rheims, to his beloved brother and fellow bishop LAMBERT of Arras, greetings with every prosperity and blessing.

Since Brother Walter was admitted to the clerical state canonically and without lawful objection, no reason stands in the way, nor does justice oppose, his promotion to be a canon, since no one can doubt that his wife committed adultery and also married another man. For, to speak according to the Apostle, after he learned that his wife had committed adultery, he was granted complete freedom to dismiss her and to fulfill any vow whatsoever, provided it be only in the Lord; except that, while she lives, he cannot take another wife.

Having heard, moreover, that in your Church investiture of prebends and altars is made by hereditary succession to a second, third, and fourth person, we are deeply astonished that your brotherhood has not resisted such a perverse and unheard-of practice. For this practice entered the holy Church through simoniacal depravity and must be abolished with all strength and uprooted with every diligence. Our Church of Rheims abhors it as wicked and regards all such investitures as void, since the Lord declares through the Prophet: “All those who have possessed God’s sanctuary as an inheritance—my God, make them like a wheel, and like chaff [Col. 0669C] before the face of the wind.” Farewell.

## LETTER LVIII. FROM THE SAME TO THE SAME.

MANASSES, by the grace of God archbishop of Rheims, to his most beloved fellow brother LAMBERT, bishop of Arras, greetings in Christ Jesus.

Because the tearful entreaties of our fellow brother and fellow bishop Manasses do not cease, neither do we cease, but plead for him with you in heart and speech. We ask, and, moved by the grief of our brother’s desolation, charitably admonish you not to delay—as we believe we have already commanded you—to place the land of the countess of Hainaut under interdict, but, for the honour of God, to perform fully and without delay what belongs to your jurisdiction.

Furthermore, we command you especially under obedience that all your abbots, monks, and clerics henceforth enter neither Cambrai nor have communion in any manner with excommunicated persons, nor hold any conversations with Walcher. For evil conversations often corrupt good morals, and, as has been reported to us, they rather encourage him to persevere in evil than call him back from error. Therefore let us correct these men, lest they be defiled by the unrighteous. Farewell; and firmly retain for yourselves the altars of those who reside at Cambrai. Farewell.

## LETTER LIX. FROM MANASSES OF CAMBRAI TO THE SAME.

To his lord LAMBERT, bishop of Arras by God’s providence, MANASSES, by the same mercy unworthy pastor [Col. 0670A] of the people of Cambrai, greetings and service.
