“If a brother is unwilling to help a brother, the consolation of both will be multiplied.” Therefore comfort me, comfort me, reverend Father—comfort me, I say—whom the accursed offspring of the people of Cambrai has betrayed as shamelessly as the countess of Hainaut does not cease to persecute me without fault or desert. Therefore, since God has left us only the spiritual sword, let us punish with the spiritual sword those through whose stormy tempests we are unable to rest either day or hour.

Since, therefore, the Apostle says, “Bear one another’s burdens,” etc., most holy Father, bear my burden: interdict the divine office throughout the land of the aforesaid countess, [Col. 0670B] who is not ashamed to dishonour God, the Roman See, the Church of Rheims, or your pastoral authority. Thus you will bind me and all who wish me well to perpetual service. Farewell; and rescue the altars of my excommunicated opponents from their unclean hands. Farewell.

## LETTER LX. FROM MANASSES OF RHEIMS TO COUNT ROBERT.

MANASSES, by the grace of God archbishop of Rheims, to his dearest and most vigorous Count ROBERT, greetings, love, and an abundance of blessing.

Remembering with what ready and gracious affection you received us in your land, we give great thanks to your affection, prepared to work according to our ability in whatever may serve friendship and your advantage. Now, if friendship consists in mutual services, you may readily measure ours from your own heart.

Moreover, when at Saint-Omer we discussed ecclesiastical benefits and affairs with you and our fellow bishops, we remember that we spoke concerning married priests and the other ecclesiastical orders, declaring that, after excommunication had been pronounced, their wives were to be seized by you and your other princes unless they withdrew from such union. But after taking counsel with our clerics, who complained against us, and recognizing that we have no canonical right, without the assent of those bishops who preside over them, to exercise authority in their parishes, [Col. 0670D] we judged it necessary to write to you more carefully. We command and admonish you neither to harass priests and the other ministers of sacred order on this account, nor to persecute their wives, nor to permit them to be injured by any of your princes—unless perhaps the bishop in whose parish they are known to be should summon you to his aid.

For we neither wish nor is it just that we should be regarded as doing wrong to any of our fellow bishops, lest, if we command something harsher than justice permits, it result in an occasion for plunder and benefit to the ecclesiastical order. For we have decreed that bishops shall most sternly confront these men on this matter in their synods; and only if, after admonition, they do not desist [Col. 0671A] from this perverse practice, shall they then call upon you as their helpers and avengers. Farewell.

## LETTER LXI. FROM JOHN AND BENEDICT, CARDINALS OF THE HOLY ROMAN CHURCH, TO LAMBERT.

JOHN and BENEDICT, cardinals and legates of the holy Roman Church, to LAMBERT, bishop of Arras, greetings and grace.

Since it is the ancient custom of our Church, and the ordinance of the sacred canons requires it, we have been sent from the Apostolic See to hold councils and to discuss and decide ecclesiastical affairs. Therefore, in order that we may carry out the task entrusted to us, we invite you and, in inviting you, command you by apostolic authority to come to Poitiers with your abbots on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of December. [Col. 0671B] For there, with the Lord’s help, we are to hold a council with you and with the other bishops and archbishops.

I, John, servant of your holiness, greet you especially. I earnestly desire your counsel and aid both in this and in other affairs; and, as a servant concerning his lord and a son concerning his father, I presume upon your favour and friendship. Farewell.

## LETTER LXII. FROM HUGH OF SOISSONS TO LAMBERT.

To his lord and father LAMBERT, venerable bishop of Arras, HUGH, officer of Soissons, unworthy to be called bishop, service always in the Lord.

I recently informed you that I continually bear in mind my desire to see you and to consult your wisdom, excellent Father. I likewise ask with all eagerness that the same favour be granted me by your fatherhood. Since I am shortly to depart, I desire, before my departure, if only once, to have your counsel and the conversation of your wisdom—which, as is fitting, I always esteem highly. I therefore beg you to appoint and determine for me a place and time where it may perhaps happen that I may see your longed-for face once more in all my life. [Col. 0671C] For I desire you as an angel of God. From you I have received many good things and have heard many good things; therefore I am and always shall be indebted to you for countless thanks. Farewell.

## LETTER LXIII. FROM HUGH, DEAN, AND ROGER AND LISIARD, ARCHDEACONS OF BEAUVAIS, TO LAMBERT.

[Col. 0671D]

To LAMBERT, by the grace of God bishop of Arras, HUGH, dean, ROGER and LISIARD, archdeacons, and the whole community of the Church of Beauvais, including the householders, together with all the people of that same city: prayers and faithful service.

Many and countless troubles, of various kinds and mutually coinciding, afflicting the Church of Beauvais, move us to send letters to your fatherhood, so that through the diligence of your vigilance we may swim out from the threatening storms into a haven of peace. Since enemies—not only invisible but visible as well—were cruelly raging against our Church and country, deprived of their pastor, [Col. 0672A] to restrain the wickedness of manifold hostility we elected Lord Stephen, archdeacon of Paris, a useful and honourable man, as our lord and bishop, by the equal wish of clergy and people and by unanimous counsel, with every simoniacal depravity removed. Though requested by us through the leading persons of our Church, he did not assent at all to our petitions, but wholly refused. Fearing, however, that we might later be burdened by the unlawful intrusion of some person imposed upon us from outside, we again resorted by common counsel to the aforesaid elect; though refusing and protesting, yet at last released to us by the Church of Paris, we honourably received him and resolved thereafter to have him as our lord and bishop. And because it is manifest to all who possess the eye of reason [Col. 0672B] that our Church cannot in any way be freed from its pressing troubles unless it is first fortified by pastoral care, we earnestly beseech your holiness to intercede for our elect with the lord pope by letters and your seal, so that through your intercession our elect may obtain the grace of consecration.

Moreover, concerning this business, we have sought and obtained from Lord Manasses, archbishop of Reims, and the other fellow-bishops who attended the council held at Soissons, letters to be directed to the supreme pontiff; for it is necessary that the Church of Beauvais, through the holy Church of Reims, certainly its mother, and through its other sisters, may by the solicitude of pastoral care attain peace—this Church which has so long [Col. 0672C] been cast down in the valley of tears, having no comforter. We also pray that you send letters of supplication concerning this business to Lord John, cardinal priest and legate of the holy Roman Church, your intimate friend, so that by your prayers we may gain him as an intercessor for us with the lord pope. Farewell.

## LETTER LXIV. LAMBERT TO BALDWIN, CLERIC OF YPRES

LAMBERT, bishop of Arras, to BALDWIN, cleric of Ypres, lately returned from the Apostolic See, and to all his associates who have a case concerning the altar of Ypres against the bishop of Thérouanne: greeting.

[Col. 0672D] In accordance with the command of the lord pope, we summon you; and in summoning you, we admonish you by apostolic authority to come before us at Arras on Friday within the octave of Epiphany—that is, the third Ides of January—before the sixth hour, so that your case concerning the aforesaid altar may there be diligently investigated and, by the mercy of almighty God, canonically determined. Farewell.

## LETTER LXV. LAMBERT TO POPE PASCHAL II

To the most reverend lord and Father of fathers, PASCHAL, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras, due submission with prayers.

The case of the bishop of Thérouanne, etc. See under Paschal II, *Patrologia*, vol. CLXIII.

## LETTER LXVI. PASCHAL TO LAMBERT

[Col. 0673A]

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother LAMBERT, bishop of Arras: greeting and apostolic blessing.

This brother, bearer of the present letter, etc. See above.

## LETTER LXVII. LAMBERT TO LANFRID, ABBOT OF ST OMER

Lambert, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras, to his beloved brother in Christ LANFRID, abbot of Saint Omer: greeting.

Let your love know that we have lately received letters from Lord Pope Paschal, who has entrusted to us the exercise of his authority in canonically examining the affair of Abbot Heribert and your own affair—that is, concerning the abbey [Col. 0673B] of Saint Omer. Therefore, by these present letters we admonish you, and by apostolic authority, whose legation we exercise in this case, command you to appear before us at Thérouanne on the Friday before the approaching Nativity of Saint John the Baptist, the fifteenth day before the Kalends of July, before the sixth hour, all evasion set aside, prepared to answer canonically regarding the matters which Heribert will bring against you.

## LETTER LXVIII. LAMBERT TO POPE PASCHAL

To the most reverend lord and Father of fathers, Pope PASCHAL, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras, due submission with prayers.

[Col. 0673C] On behalf of our venerable metropolitan, Lord Manasses, archbishop of Reims, etc. See under Paschal, *Patrologia*, vol. CLXIII.

## LETTER LXIX. MANASSES OF REIMS TO LAMBERT

MANASSES, by God’s grace archbishop of Reims, to LAMBERT, venerable bishop of Arras: greeting and an abundance of love.

By the command of divine authority we are admonished to grieve over the miseries of others as though they were our own, and to entreat the mercy of the Almighty for the obstinacy of the perverse, that they may return to their senses, and that He may deign to deliver the afflicted from the hands of those wicked men. For concerning the keeper of the keys of heaven, when he was confined in the filth of a prison, the apostolic reading relates thus: “Peter indeed was kept [Col. 0673D] in prison, but prayer was made without ceasing by the Church to God for him.” And Paul, the trumpet of heaven, teaches us by his own example to sympathize with the sufferings of the wretched, when he says to the Corinthians: “Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?”

Therefore we greatly grieve, and admonish your charity also to grieve, over the exceedingly grievous captivity of Lord Hugh, bishop of Châlons, our father and lord in age and wisdom, and pre-eminent in nobility. Alberic of Meslano holds him bound in tyrannical captivity—and, shame upon it!—within that very bishopric of his. For this deed we have separated from communion of the Church both him and those by whose counsel and assistance he captured the bishop; we have ceased to sing and to sound our bells. Yet, singing the course of all the hours and Mass in commemoration of the blessed Apostle Peter, we celebrate them at a certain altar of his, so that the Lord by His grace may rescue our fellow-brother from captivity. We pray and admonish you to do likewise at some altar of Saint Peter, and to command that this be done similarly in all religious communities; and that a private Mass likewise be celebrated at the high altar. Throughout the whole bishopric, however, the divine office is to be forbidden, except in the communities where, as stated above, it is sung; and excommunication is to be pronounced daily against the aforesaid evildoers until either repentance corrects them or the divine sentence punishes them. Farewell.

## LETTER LXX. LAMBERT TO MANASSES OF REIMS

[Col. 0674B]

To the honourable lord and most dear father MANASSES, by God’s grace archbishop of Reims, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras: love and eternal salvation in God.

We recently received letters sealed with your seal from a certain layman unknown to us in appearance and name; and, opening them before our brethren, we found that our venerable fellow-bishop Lord Hugh of Châlons was being held captive—a matter which grieves us exceedingly. Afterwards, when they said that on this account we should cease from divine praises, our brethren doubted whether such letters had proceeded from the seat of your discretion, both because the messenger was unknown to everyone [Col. 0674C] and because this command accords in no way with the Old and New Testaments.

For in the Old Testament it is written: “They cried unto the Lord when they were troubled, and He delivered them from their distresses.” He did not command them to cease, but to cry out. And in the New: “When Peter was kept in prison, prayer was made without ceasing by the Church to God for him.” For while the Church prayed and did not cease, the Lord sent His angel and delivered him from the hands of Herod and from all the expectation of the Jewish people. And the Lord says in the Gospel: “Men ought always to pray and never to lose heart.”

Furthermore, they allege to us that when Lord Hugh, primate of Lyons and legate of the Apostolic See, was held captive by Archambault of Bourbon, he specially excommunicated Archambault, caused his land [Col. 0674D] and castles to cease from divine services, and placed the entire province under interdict. Likewise Pope Urban, a man of venerable memory, in a letter sent to our lord Archbishop Rainald, your predecessor, for the correction of Lord Philip, king of the French, wrote among other things concerning the seizure of the bishop of Chartres:

“Apply the same earnestness also for the rescue of our fellow-brother, the bishop of Chartres. But if he who seized him should disdain to obey your admonitions, subject both him to excommunication, and forbid the divine office in every castle in which he holds him and throughout his land, lest similar outrages henceforth be dared against men of this order. As you love your order, let all of you strive with all your might to hasten this.”

[Col. 0675A] Likewise, when we were making haste to the Council of Clermont and were held captive by Guarnerius of Pont, the aforesaid venerable pope wrote to Richer, archbishop of Sens, and commanded that, for as long as Guarnerius held us, he and his land should be subjected to excommunication. [Note: [Col. 0675D] See above, col. 646.] Likewise, from the decrees of the Council of Clermont: “If anyone seizes or imprisons a bishop, let him be subject to perpetual infamy and thereafter bear arms no more.” And all cried: “Let it be done.”

We have sent these examples to you so that, in these perilous times which have come upon us in great abundance, your metropolitan see may strive to do and proclaim what the whole province may reasonably undertake to do. Reverend father and lord, fare well in God our salvation; and write back to us what seems to you just and reasonable concerning [Col. 0675B] these matters.

## LETTER LXXI. MANASSES OF REIMS TO LAMBERT

MANASSES, by God’s grace archbishop of Reims, to LAMBERT, venerable bishop of Arras, and to the other brethren of the Church of Arras who are with him: to magnify God in His mercies.

Strive to render thanksgiving to the Lord and to sing praises without ceasing, for He has turned our mourning and sorrow into joy and exultation. For He has been gloriously honoured and has magnificently delivered His Christ from bonds. That Antichrist who held him captive, while fleeing, had taken him into the bishopric of Toul. [Col. 0675C] There, when the bishop of Toul learned that he was present, he summoned Duke Theodoric and the other leading men of his bishopric; as they discussed among themselves the liberation of the bishop and decided that the undertaking must be boldly pursued, that condemned man who held him perceived it. Fearing the destruction of his castle and that they would pronounce him infamous and unlawful, he set the bishop free. He has already restored part of all that belonged to the bishop or to his people; and he pledged that he would restore the remaining part at his own house in Châlons and render him justice.

Therefore we wish all of you to be admonished that, as you multiplied prayers to the Lord for his release from prison, so you should remember to multiply praises and magnify God for his liberation. Farewell.

## LETTER LXXII. BALDRIC OF NOYON TO LAMBERT

[Col. 0675D]

To his beloved brother in Christ and lord LAMBERT, venerable bishop of Arras, BALDRIC, by the same grace bishop of Noyon: may you always possess the grace of the Holy Spirit.

Most reverend Father, we have already written to you concerning the monks of Saint Quentin of the Mount who are to be ordained. Now we write to you again, humbly beseeching and asking in the grace of the Holy Spirit that you promote these present clerics of ours to sacred orders: Baldwin to be an acolyte; Levolf, Evrard, and Gislebert to the rank of subdeacon; Bernard [Col. 0676A] and Isambert to the office of deacon; and Berner to be a priest. Farewell.

## LETTER LXXIII. I., TREASURER OF THE CHURCH OF ST QUENTIN, TO LAMBERT

To the venerable bishop of Arras, LAMBERT, I., treasurer of the church of Blessed Quentin: favour before God and men.

We wish your fatherhood to know that we have granted this boy full freedom at the request of our friends, namely Guenemar of Laon and Galand. We ask that you graciously grant him, if it please you, whatever he may humbly request from you. Let this be a sign to you: when you were travelling to Rome this year, you met our cleric Fulk at the gate of Ham. We were unable to affix a seal to the letter, because we lost it in the fires themselves. [Col. 0676B] Farewell.

## LETTER LXXIV. BALDRIC OF NOYON TO LAMBERT

To Lord LAMBERT, by God’s grace bishop of Arras, BALDRIC, by the same grace humble bishop of Noyon: himself wholly in the Lord.

We know that it has not escaped your notice that Master Peter held a benefice in our church and afterwards, by the ordering grace of God, renounced the world in your bishopric. Since he has lately chosen for himself a suitable and quiet place in your diocese, we commend him kindly to your fatherhood and earnestly ask you to take charge of him, both in orders and [Col. 0676C] in other matters. Farewell.

## LETTER LXXV. MANASSES OF REIMS TO LAMBERT

MANASSES, by God’s grace archbishop of Reims, to his most reverend brother and fellow-bishop Lord LAMBERT of Arras: greeting with all affection.

Since the abbot of the monastery of Forest had entered upon the way of all flesh, the abbot of Saint-Riquier and I., archdeacon of the Church of Amiens, lately sent us letters reporting that the brethren of that monastery had elected as their abbot a certain monk of Saint-Riquier named Robert. Giving him trustworthy testimony, they affirmed that his election was canonical and made with unanimous agreement. The countess of Ponthieu and the other men of that land likewise bore testimony on his behalf, affirmed that the election was canonical, and asked us to consecrate him. But, because that place does not sufficiently abound in necessities, nor is access to us from it easy, we command and ask your brotherhood, since it is nearer to you, to consecrate him abbot unless perhaps you hear something concerning him or his election that conflicts with the sacred canons. [Col. 0676D] Farewell.

## LETTER LXXVI. ROBERT, COUNT OF FLANDERS, TO LAMBERT

To Lord LAMBERT, venerable bishop of Arras, ROBERT, count of Flanders: greetings and friendship.

[Col. 0677A] Let your discretion know that I have done homage to the German emperor, because otherwise I could not possess in full the fief which I ought to hold from him by ancestral right, especially since I perceived that, apart from this, the peace of our country could not be restored. Yet this was done with my authority and obedience to the Roman pontiff and his Church, as well as to the Church of Reims, preserved, and without violation of my Christianity or lawful fidelity; moreover, I have in no way thereby incurred any presumption against your see and dignity, or any injury to them. Therefore I entrust to your love peace and complete security; and I most certainly promise that henceforth I shall in every matter commit myself to the most salutary counsel of your holiness concerning what we have done or shall do in the aforesaid matters. Farewell.

## LETTER LXXVII. EUREMAR, PATRIARCH OF JERUSALEM, TO LAMBERT

[Col. 0677B]

EUREMAR, by God’s grace patriarch of Jerusalem, to his most beloved spiritual father LAMBERT, bishop of Arras: brotherly love in Christ.

Dearest Father, I offer you every thanks because, while I was under the hand of your humility, you loved and instructed me with fatherly affection. Therefore, as a father and teacher, I earnestly urge you not to forget the friendship and love then mutually praised between us. For although separated by the expanse of lands and seas, I cannot, to my sorrow, behold your sweetness with bodily sight; nevertheless, with the eyes of my mind I always behold your goodness and charity. [Col. 0677C] For, God knows, above all others I love and embrace you.

Therefore, most dear one, having the greatest confidence in your goodwill, I ask you, if it please you, to help lighten the burden of obedience which you know has been laid upon me, fulfilling the apostolic command: “Bear one another’s burdens” (Galatians 6:1), etc. If it pleases your excellency to command anything of us, you will find me, according to my ability, most ready in every respect to comply with your will. In prayers and in other benefits, whatever pleasing thing our frailty can accomplish by divine clemency, know that you share in it as a most beloved master and brother.

Moreover, from the blessing of the Holy Sepulchre we send you one gold ring and two crystal flasks filled with balsam. Fare well, [Col. 0677D] and pray for us and for the holy city Jerusalem.

Given on the third day before the Nones of April.

Afterwards followed the patriarch’s leaden bull; upon its inner circumference these words were written in Greek: **ὁ ἅγιος τάφος τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ**, “the holy tomb of the Lord Jesus Christ”; and on the outer circumference, in Latin: “The seal of Euremar, patriarch of Jerusalem.”

And in the margin: “Received on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of December. Sent from Jerusalem to Arras in the year of Christ our Lord 1104.”

## LETTER LXXVIII. LAMBERT TO EUREMAR

To the honourable lord and truly beloved EUREMAR, patriarch of Jerusalem, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy [Col. 0678A] bishop of Arras: that which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the human heart.

We have already often rendered you thanks for your gifts through our household servants, and have earnestly instructed you to report back to us concerning your condition and manner of life. But since no one has yet given us assurance concerning your condition and health, we have not thought it burdensome to greet you through our beloved brother A., archdeacon of Thérouanne, and to remind you to remember us in your prayers at the holy Resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ. Fare well. Reverend sir, because you have taken care to send us devout and honourable gifts, may recompense be rendered to you in the resurrection of the righteous. The brethren who are with us greet you: Lord Clarembald, [Col. 0678B] our archdeacon, and Cono, a religious man of Arida Gamantia.

## LETTER LXXIX. POPE PASCHAL II TO COUNT EUSTACE

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the distinguished count EUSTACE: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those things which are begun with good principles, etc. See under Paschal II, *Patrologia*, vol. CLXIII.

## LETTER LXXX. PASCHAL TO MANASSES OF REIMS

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother MANASSES, bishop of Reims: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 0678C] Our brother, the bishop of Arras, complains concerning the archpriest Guarinfrid, etc. See above.

## LETTER LXXXI. MANASSES OF REIMS TO GUARINFRED, ARCHPRIEST

MANASSES, by God’s grace archbishop of Reims, to GUARINFRED, archpriest: greeting and peace, if he obeys.

Our brother Lambert, bishop of Arras, complains that you violently seize ten churches belonging to his jurisdiction and their revenues, situated in the territory of Arras—namely Vals in Artois, Noeroil, Cadom, Perolville, Cauvennicurt, Frasnoi, Serum, Saudemont, Sclusa, Ahilcurt—and the chapels appurtenant to them; and that you have for a long time presumed obstinately to retain them with their revenues. We have received apostolic letters concerning this matter. Therefore we direct and command you to relinquish those churches to our aforesaid fellow-brother Lambert, bishop of Arras, and to make satisfaction by the approaching Sunday on which “The Mercy of the Lord” is sung. If you delay to do what we command and presume to stand against the decrees of the Apostolic See, you shall be subject to anathema on that Sunday already fixed for you. [Col. 0678D] Farewell.

## LETTER LXXXII. PASCHAL TO MANASSES

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable [Col. 0679A] brother and fellow-bishop MANASSES of Reims: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Your love had informed us, etc. See above.

## LETTER LXXXIII. PASCHAL TO LAMBERT

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother LAMBERT of Arras: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The bearers of the present letter, Robert and A., etc. See under Paschal.

## LETTER LXXXIV. RICHARD, APOSTOLIC LEGATE, TO ROBERT, COUNT OF FLANDERS

RICHARD, by God’s grace bishop of Albano and legate of the Apostolic [Col. 0679B] See, to ROBERT, distinguished count of the Flemings: greeting.

We believe that it cannot be unknown to you, count of his own city as you are, what reputation, honour, and religious devotion our intimate brother Lambert, bishop of Arras, possesses, since even those most distant know it. Indeed, he is so worthy of recommendation to the Apostolic See that it regards him with a certain prerogative as pre-eminent among the other bishops of Gaul. We therefore commend to your prudence and power such a man, so venerable, that you may protect him, by the right of power entrusted to you by God, against all who plot any act of rebellion against him.

Moreover, regard as excommunicated Robert, the so-called cleric of Arras who is joined to a widow and obstinately rebellious against his bishop, together with all accomplices of his party, until he is reconciled with his bishop. If the bishop determines that measures must be maintained against the wickedness of clerics, let him find in you not a supporter of wickedness but a defender of justice. [Col. 0679C] Farewell.

## LETTER LXXXV. LAMBERT TO POPE PASCHAL II

To the most reverend lord, Father of fathers, Pope PASCHAL, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras: due submission with prayers.

For our religious brother John, abbot of Mont-Saint-Éloi, we beseech the concern of your holiness, that you may deign to hear him fatherly in his cases. We also ask that you confirm by your privilege both him and his successors in the place and rank which he now holds, as well as property lawfully given to the Church, canonically possessed, or, by God’s mercy, yet to be given. We have also granted to the canons who live and shall live there regularly and without private property the right of canonical election upon the death of an abbot, while preserving in all things the right of the bishop of Arras. [Col. 0679D] May the Holy Trinity, our God, keep your holiness safe for a longer time.

## LETTER LXXXVI. THE SAME TO THE SAME

To the most reverend lord and Father of fathers, Pope PASCHAL, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras: due reverence with prayers.

Humbled at the feet of your holiness, we implore the kindness of [Col. 0680A] your fatherhood that, according to the decrees of the holy Fathers and the enactments of the canons, you may be willing to hear and treat us justly in all matters. For, God being favourable, we have striven and continue to strive to order ecclesiastical dispensations concerning prebends and altars purely and canonically.

Through the faithful bearer of this letter, Drogo, son and subdeacon of our Church, we wrote to your excellency asking permission to appoint an abbot over eight monks in the church called Fescherias, under the title of Saint Praejectus. This church had been freely possessed by Lord Gerard, our predecessor as bishop, and has hitherto in all respects been subject to the holy Church of Arras. Therefore, because you received our petition and confirmed to us by the authority of your privilege that we should appoint there an abbot according to the Rule of Saint Benedict, in obedience to the see of Arras, we offer manifold thanks to your ecclesiastical administration.

But afterwards Guibert, abbot of Saint Praejectus, complained to you that I was taking away this church of ours for myself as though it were his cell. Consequently, summoned on the appointed day by letters of your authority to the see of Reims, where you had commanded the archbishop to determine this case canonically, I came into the presence of the archbishop and the fellow-bishops of the province, intending to pursue the justice of this case. How the matter was brought to judgment before the archbishop of Reims and the provincial bishops, and how the aforesaid abbot, distrusting his claim to justice, refused to undergo judgment, Lord Archbishop [Col. 0680C] has, as we believe, already reported to you in his letters.

Therefore, again imploring the concern of your holiness, we desire that you stand with us and that you be willing to maintain what you confirmed by the authority of your privilege. And we are the more astonished and troubled why, when you have not yet found in us “yes and no,” you were willing so quickly to summon and weary us over such a matter. May the Holy Trinity, our God, preserve unharmed for a longer time your daily solicitude, labouring and praying for the holy catholic Church.

## LETTER LXXXVII. THE SAME TO THE SAME

To the most reverend lord and Father of fathers, Pope PASCHAL, [Col. 0680D] LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras: due submission with prayers.

Since it has pleased your concern, which you bear toward all Churches, to determine disputes between us and our clerics according to canonical provisions and the decrees of the saints, to the honour of the Christian religion, we render thanks to God and to your holiness. Furthermore, we beseech your justice not to hear against us, to the injury of our Church, the messenger of Count Eustace, our cleric named Guago, who acts unjustly concerning our altars and churches. Geoffrey, bishop of Paris, formerly archdeacon of Arras, freely possessed them in his personal benefice for thirty years and more, and in our days annually paid the episcopal dues.

We also wish your holiness to know [Col. 0681A] that the aforesaid count permits neither us, nor the archbishop of Reims, nor even your letters, sent to him a second time by you, to possess what is ours; rather, both he and his officers take these things from us. Therefore we have already excluded him from entry into the churches and excommunicated his officers as plunderers of ecclesiastical property; and we ask you to confirm our excommunication. Concerning Robert’s case, about which you wrote to us, whatever good and just assistance you can provide, we shall endure for the peace of the Church. Write to us your definitive judgment, with the honour and judgment of the holy Roman Church preserved. Concerning the abbot of Ghent and the other questions which our faithful subdeacon has told you, answer him. [Col. 0681B] May the Holy Trinity, our God, preserve your holiness unharmed for a longer time.

## LETTER LXXXVIII. PASCHAL TO LAMBERT

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother LAMBERT, bishop of Arras: greeting and blessing.

Certain clerics of your Church, etc. See under Paschal.

## LETTER LXXXIX. LAMBERT TO PASCHAL

To the most reverend lord and Father of fathers, PASCHAL, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras: due submission with prayers.

We ask your paternal reverence to be pleased to hear these brethren [Col. 0681C] of the community of Saint Amatus at Douai concerning their petition: namely, that you confirm by the authority of your privilege the liberty of their Church and its goods lawfully given or to be given and canonically possessed, lest the hands of invaders, by whom it is hard pressed on every side, have an opportunity utterly to devastate a Church subject to our obedience. As for the dean, in whose hands the care lies, who has not come to you: believe that not presumption but old age and infirmity are the cause. May the Holy Trinity, our God, keep your fatherhood unharmed for a longer time.

## LETTER XC. THE SAME TO THE SAME

To the most reverend lord and most dear Father of fathers, [Col. 0681D] Pope PASCHAL, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras: the unceasing consolation of the Holy Spirit.

Abbess Fulgendis, sister and daughter of our Church and bearer of this letter, earnestly asked that she be commended through us to your holiness, so that you may deign to confirm the present abbess in the place, profession, and rank which she now holds, by the weight of your authority, while preserving in all respects the right and canonical ordering of the bishop of Arras. The site of the monastery called Strum and the altar of Hamartville, as my predecessor Lord Bishop Gerard granted and confirmed by his writing, we also grant, in hope and love of religion, for possession by this present abbess and the abbesses succeeding her, canonically elected and to be canonically promoted in the monastery over which she is now known to preside, [Col. 0682A] and who shall live without secular disturbance. We likewise ask you to strengthen the other property and possessions justly acquired or to be acquired, because of the harassment and plundering of wicked men. May the Holy Trinity, our God, preserve unharmed for a longer time your solicitude, labouring and praying for the holy catholic Church.

## LETTER XCI. THE SAME TO THE SAME

To the most reverend lord and Father of fathers, Pope PASCHAL, LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras: due reverence with prayers.

[Col. 0682B] Our brother and son of the Church, Cono, bearer of this letter, asked us to obtain from your mercy that you would be willing to confirm the church called Rochennias and the place in which he lives with the brethren in the liberty with which we have endowed them. For we have granted and confirmed in writing the aforesaid places to the superior and brethren who there serve God devoutly and religiously, who live and shall live canonically and without private property, free from every payment of cathedraticum, except that on Maundy Thursday they shall pay twelve pence into the bishop’s hand. And we have ordained that the aforesaid brethren shall remain under the proper and special subjection, ordering, and protection of the bishop of Arras. May the Lord preserve unharmed for a longer time your holiness, labouring for the holy Church. [Col. 0682C]

## LETTER XCII. LAMBERT TO ANSELM OF CANTERBURY

To the honourable lord and truly beloved ANSELM, by God’s appointment archbishop of Canterbury, LAMBERT, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Arras: that which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the human heart.

With great desire I have desired to know concerning your condition and health. I write to your fatherhood, most sweet to me, asking that you deign to give us assurance concerning these matters by your letter. I earnestly desire that your holiness, with contrite heart and humble spirit, pray that you may remember me, a sinner, at the Lord’s table itself and in your holy prayers, and obtain for me from God forgiveness of sins. May your holy and religious manner of life fare well in the Lord, best of fathers, for a long time and always; and we earnestly ask that, on our behalf, you greet Lord Baldric of Tournai, your friend and a son of your holiness.

## LETTER XCIII. ANSELM TO LAMBERT

To LAMBERT, venerable bishop of Arras and most beloved friend, ANSELM, servant of the Church of Canterbury: greeting and faithful prayers.

I thank your reverend love for the concern it has for me in so greatly wishing to know of my health. I tell you, therefore, [Col. 0683A] that by God’s grace I am sound in body, but suffer from continual weakness. As for your request that I remember you in our prayers, know certainly that, although my prayers are worthless, I nevertheless remember you in them daily and, God granting, shall continue to do so. May almighty God always defend you by His grace from every evil and graciously bestow His consolation upon you.

## LETTER XCIV. POPE PASCHAL TO HENRY, ABBOT OF ST VAAST

PASCHAL, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son HENRY, abbot of Saint Vaast: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The report which we recently heard concerning you, etc. See under Paschal, *Patrologia*, vol. CLXIII.

## LETTER XCV. BALDRIC, BISHOP OF NOYON, TO LAMBERT

[Col. 0683B]

To Lord LAMBERT, venerable bishop of Arras, BALDRIC, by God’s grace bishop of Noyon: greeting and brotherly affection.

This poor woman, one of our parishioners, devoutly asks to receive the veil. We therefore ask your serenity, if it please you, to veil her and consecrate her as a handmaid of Christ. Farewell.

## LETTER XCVI. GODEFRID OF AMIENS TO LAMBERT

To Lord LAMBERT, by God’s grace bishop of Arras, GODEFRID, by the same grace of God bishop of Amiens: greeting.

We entrust to you, released from our jurisdiction, this priest of ours, Theoderannus, who has left our bishopric under compulsion of necessity and wishes to remain in your bishopric, on the condition that he owes and renders to you the obedience that he owed to our Church and to us. [Col. 0683C] Farewell.

## LETTER XCVII. LAMBERT TO POPE PASCHAL

To the most reverend lord and Father of fathers, Pope PASCHAL, LAMBERT, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Arras: due reverence with prayers.

Concerning the grievous and lamentable oppression of the holy Church of Reims and its honourable metropolitan, Lord Ralph, we most earnestly ask the concern of your holiness which you bear toward all Churches, that by your wise counsel and the aid of your authority you may strive to restore good peace to the aforesaid Church, both before God and before men. For we hope that, through the envoys of Louis, king of the Franks, if your vigilance is willing to give attention, you will be able both to secure peace for the Church of Reims and to obtain for its metropolitan the king’s favour and friendship. [Col. 0683D] May your holiness fare well in the Lord, and for a long time, and always; and deign to pray for me, a sinner.

### Letter XCVIII. William, Archbishop of Rouen, to Lambert

WILLIAM, by the grace of God Archbishop of Rouen, to his most beloved lord and brother LAMBERT, bishop of Arras, present and eternal salvation.

[Col. 0684A] We warmly commend to your religious care our most beloved son Walter, since it has pleased him to live with you, on account of his honourable character. For, because he was unwilling to comply with the vices of certain persons, he incurred their hatred rather for truth’s sake than through any fault of his own. Farewell.

### Letter XCIX. Lambert to Daimbert, Archbishop of Sens

To the honourable lord and truly beloved DAIMBERT, by God’s appointment Archbishop of Sens, LAMBERT, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Arras: that which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man.

We humbly entreat you to deign graciously to accept the gloves honourably decorated with spun gold and the hand-towel which we have taken care to send you for the service of your dignity. [Col. 0684B] Fare well, reverend Father; and remember me, a sinner, in your holy prayers, especially at the Lord’s table, that God, the Father of mercies and of all consolation, may mercifully deign to bring me, a sinner, out of the pit of misery, from the mire of filth, and from the prison of this life, into salvation.

### Letter C. Henry, King of England, to Lambert

HENRY, by the grace of God King of the English and Duke of the Normans, to LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras: greeting and friendship.

I thank you for what you sent me through D., your clerk; and I wish you henceforth to have confidence in me in this matter, [Col. 0684C] and I shall gladly act on your behalf. Farewell.

### Letter CI. O., Cardinal of the Holy Roman Church, to Lambert

O., priest-cardinal of the holy Roman Church, to his dearest Father LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras: greeting and good peace.

Having recently departed from the side of the lord pope, I received instructions to be communicated to you and to my fellow bishops. Therefore, by the authority of him who sent me, we exhort your belovedness to be present with us at Corbie on the fourth Sunday of Lent. Farewell.

### Letter CII. Odo of Cambrai to Lambert

To Lord LAMBERT, by the grace of God Bishop of Arras, ODO, unworthy servant of the Church of Cambrai, [Col. 0684D] faithful prayers in the Lord.

With respect to this brother named Roger, I grant you his obedience, so far as lies within my power, if it pleases you to retain him. Farewell.

### Letter CIII. The Community of Anchin to Lambert

To its venerable lord and reverend father, Lord LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras, the humble community of the brothers of Anchin: humble greetings and service, with the assurance of due submission.

Let your venerable fatherhood know that we all granted to the aforesaid Lord Gelduin, formerly our abbot, full permission in every respect to resign the abbacy, as you learned either from himself or from Lord Amand, [Col. 0685A] our prior, and the brothers whom we sent with him. We ask, however, that you attribute it to simplicity rather than arrogance that we did not send you, at first, letters of this our consent together with them. For, overcome by great grief, we unknowingly omitted this. Nor indeed did we grant him such permission lightly, or at his first request; but because, unless we granted it, he threatened emphatically that he would depart, we preferred to retain him at least in this manner rather than let him go altogether. Fare well, and we ask you, lord, to remember us.

### Letter CIV. The Same Community to the Same Recipient

To the venerable Lord LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras, the humble community of Anchin: greeting through the propitious grace of God, with the due submission [Col. 0685B] and reverence.

By common consent we have chosen this present brother of ours, Lord Robert, as abbot for ourselves, and have sent him to your fatherhood to be consecrated, beseeching you to approve and confirm what we have begun in him. May the Lord preserve you in safety.

### Letter CV. Lambert to King Louis

To his honourable lord and truly beloved king, LOUIS, LAMBERT, priest of the holy Church of Arras: to live and reign in the Lord Jesus Christ, the only Son of God the Father, King of kings and Lord of all rulers.

We beseech the gentleness of your highness, [Col. 0685C] in which we greatly trust, to grant this bearer of the present letter, our messenger, an opportunity to report freely to you what we send. Fare well always in the Lord God; and through him by whom kings reign, may justice and an abundance of peace arise in your days.

### Letter CVI. Lambert to Ralph of Reims

To the reverend Father and Lord RALPH, by God’s appointment Archbishop of Reims, LAMBERT, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Arras: eternal joy and gladness in the Holy Spirit.

We write to you on behalf of our brother Henry, abbot of Saint-Vaast, asking that, should any accuser or whisperer come to you in order to trouble him, [Col. 0685D] you receive no person’s accusation nor hear any voice, unless an appeal has been made to you, until you have informed us of the persons accusing him—or rather, of the disturbers of Christian peace and of the holy canons. Fare well, my reverend Father and lord, with all who truly love you; and pray for us.

### Letter CVII. Lambert to the Priest Pomon

To Lord POMON, a religious priest, beloved of God, and to all his community, LAMBERT, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Arras and unworthy priest: that which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man.

Since my fellow countrymen, the honourable priests L. and A., gave me much information concerning the praiseworthy conduct of you and your [Col. 0686A] sons, they have given me, as it were, confidence to seek from the affection of your brotherhood what we request. We earnestly ask that you deign to send us, written down in your truthful hand, what was sung and what was read in the visible celebration of the Mass, as it is called. A canon, your neighbour at Saint Peter’s, who had become a monk, saw and heard blessed Augustine celebrating this in the confession-chapel of the monastery of the aforesaid apostle, at the altar of his own tomb.

The aforesaid brothers testified that, in that office, they retained only the Communion: “This is my body, which shall be delivered for you,” and that it was sung there. Fare well, reverend [Col. 0686B] and beloved Father, in the only Son of God the Father, our Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ; and pray for us. Record also, as is customary, the manner, time, and hour of the vision, together with the year of the Lord’s Incarnation and the indiction; likewise who was then pontiff in the holy Roman Catholic and Apostolic See, and who was then head of the Church of Pavia.

### Letter CVIII. Lambert to G., Archdeacon of Paris

To his brother and lord G., Archdeacon of Paris, deservedly most beloved, LAMBERT, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Arras: that which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man.

Since charity is the bond of perfection and the mistress of all virtues, and, according to blessed Bishop Fulgentius, [Col. 0686C] he who walks in charity neither errs nor sins, we are greatly and exceedingly surprised why you recently wished, so obstinately—if I may venture to say so—and so contentiously at last to retain, though not without a condition, the hand-towel which we had sent to that servant of God, the abbot of Melun, your brother, whose death we had not yet heard of.

Therefore, my beloved brother and lord, do not henceforth do such a thing concerning our desires and wishes; but do not neglect to claim for yourselves, as by a certain hereditary right, the small gift which we sent with good will and full charity to the aforesaid servant of God, both on account of his affection and because of our devout gift. Fare well, and pray for us.

### Letter CIX. Lambert to Richard of Albano

[Col. 0686D]

To the honourable lord and friend RICHARD of Albano, among bishops and above all others, LAMBERT, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Arras and unworthy priest: eternal joy and gladness in the Holy Spirit.

Trusting in the abundant loving-kindness which your goodness bears toward us, we commend to you this bearer of the present letter, humbly asking you to hear him attentively and, for God’s love and at our request, to let him experience in the justice of his cause the benefit of our advocacy. Fare well, my reverend Father and lord, in the Lord God our salvation; and pray for us.

### Letter CX. Lambert to F., His Full Brother and Brother by the Same Mother

[Col. 0687A]

LAMBERT, by God’s mercy Bishop of Arras, to F., his brother by the same father and mother: to wrestle with the angel as Jacob wrestled, but, when dawn rises, not to let the angel go until he deserves to receive a blessing from him.

Since the divine law pursues, follows up, and demands promises more strictly than debts, no true Christian should be rash or deceitful in making promises, lest he be judged guilty or false for not fulfilling what he promised. But how great a sin lying is to the soul, let us hear with fear and trembling from the prophet, who says: “A lying mouth kills the soul.” Hence the most holy King David and most truthful prophet [Col. 0687B] says: “You will destroy all who speak falsehood”; and again: “Men of blood and deceit shall not live out half their days.” And the Lord Jesus says in the Gospel: “For by your words you shall be justified, and by your words you shall be condemned.” Another Scripture also says: “Life and death are in the hands of the tongue.”

Concerning this detestable and deadly vice, let us hear the sound counsel of Holy Scripture: “He who guards his mouth guards his soul.” The apostle Paul also, herald of our salvation and learned physician of our infirmity, instructs the whole Catholic Church, saying: “Do not lie to one another, putting off the old man with his deeds and putting on the new man, who is created according to God in righteousness and holiness of truth.”

Let us therefore correct, according to the healing precepts of so many [Col. 0687C] Scriptures, the wicked and perverse habits of lying. Let us deceive no one; let us promise no one what we are unwilling to do. For while we cautiously and deliberately lie to our neighbour, we kill ourselves and our souls, and imitate the apostate angel, concerning whom Christ Jesus says in the most holy Gospel: “He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth; he is a liar and its father.” For the devil is the father of lying, not by begetting it, but by inventing it for himself through pride. The bearer of this letter will privately explain to you and to my beloved sister why I wished to write so much about lying. Fare well in the Lord, and strive so to pass through temporal goods that you do not lose eternal ones.

### Letter CXI. Richard, Legate of the Apostolic See, to Lambert

[Col. 0687D]

RICHARD, by the grace of God Bishop of Albano, though unworthy minister and legate of the Apostolic See, to his venerable brother LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras: greeting.

We have heard that an abhorrent practice, forbidden by the sacred canons, has grown up in your Church: namely, that certain churches have three or more persons appointed as principal incumbents, and that, upon the death of one, the others succeed to his share, and so on until the last. Yet we recall having read in the commentaries of blessed Augustine that one church ought to have only one priest. We therefore prohibit this, and command you by apostolic authority [Col. 0688A] to prohibit it firmly.

Further, concerning usurers, we command by apostolic authority that, if their claimants can prove by the testimony of witnesses that they have repaid them their money and the interest, you are not to doubt that they have fulfilled the judicial procedure and that the interest must accordingly be repaid.

### Letter CXII. Gilduin to Lambert

To Lord LAMBERT, by God’s grace Bishop of Arras, worthy of reverence by every right, but to be embraced by me above all others with special affection, GILDUIN, servant of your holiness: true health of soul and body in Christ Jesus.

The love and grace of affection which your holiness deigned to show toward my lowliness [Col. 0688B] when I deserved to be elevated to acquaintance with your friendship, I still feel to be undiminished and desire to remain so. For unless you greatly loved my peace, you would not have answered as you did when our brothers of Anchin asked you such things concerning me.

For I learned from Lord Drogo, who reported to me on your behalf, that the brothers of Anchin had again elected me as their abbot and had consulted your fatherhood whether you would assist them in such a matter. You replied that you could not do so, because I was no longer your monk nor living in your diocese; but you have now sent Lord Drogo to inquire carefully what our will might be in this matter.

Therefore we render manifold thanks to your holy charity because you do not wish to disturb the peace of our seclusion, [Col. 0688C] and by every prayer we most earnestly beseech you that I may always have you as my helper and defender in this matter. For truly, God being witness, we have no other wish concerning this or any other abbey, nor, with God’s aid, do we wish to have one beyond the wish we had on the day when we resigned it. And if such a wish were present, assuredly the health of the body, which is already failing, would by no means be equal to so great a burden. Farewell.

### Letter CXIII. Lambert to F., Abbot

LAMBERT, by God’s mercy Bishop of Arras, to his brother F., abbot, beloved in Christ: to walk in the Spirit and not fulfil the desires of the flesh, but always to think and do what God has commanded him.

[Col. 0688D] Since we recently sent you our letters and commanded you under obedience to come to us last Thursday, and you have not yet come, nor sent word why you did not come, we do not bear this as patiently as we have hitherto. We therefore command you and firmly order you, by the authority through which we preside over you, to put aside every excuse and not delay presenting yourself to us on the coming Thursday or, alternatively, on the following Friday before the sixth hour.

For we have to confer with you concerning your religious observance and the conduct of your monastery, because Lord Richard, the cardinal and bishop, legate of the Apostolic See, has resolved to hold a council before the feast of Saint Remigius and has commanded the abbots of the province of Reims to attend. Since obedience is better [Col. 0689A] than sacrifice; since, according to blessed Gregory, it is a practice of upright conduct that no one should command obedience who does not know how to show it to superiors; and since true obedience admits of no delay: we forbid you both place and seat as abbot unless you diligently endeavour to fulfil what we command.

### Letter CXIV. A., Prior of Anchin, to Lambert

To Lord LAMBERT, by God’s grace Bishop of Arras, Brother A., Prior of Anchin, and the flock dwelling under him: the service of due submission.

Since, lord Father, as you know, we were disappointed in the election by which we had elected Lord Gilduin, obedient to your command, and on the appointed day having gathered together almost all the sons of our Church, [Col. 0689B] after much deliberation we at last, with the assistance of the Holy Spirit—whose presence in our counsels we implored with tears—elected by common counsel Lord Alvisus, prior of the church of Saint-Vaast, to be our pastor.

We therefore ask your clemency to approach Lord Lambert, abbot of Saint-Bertin, concerning this matter, so that, because Alvisus is a professed monk of his monastery, he may deign to consent to our wishes by granting us the man for whom the unanimous agreement of the sounder part of the whole chapter has cried out. Farewell.

### Letter CXV. Lambert to John, Bishop of the Morini

To the venerable Lord JOHN, by God’s grace Bishop of the Morini, LAMBERT of Arras, by God’s mercy, [Col. 0689C] if he be anything: to fare well, well and always, in the only Son of God the Father.

Because it is written, “A brother helping a brother, both shall be consoled,” we beseech your holiness, in which we greatly trust—indeed, presume—that you confirm and strengthen with us the election which the brothers of Anchin have made of your son Alvisus, prior of Saint-Vaast; or that, by the authority given you by God, you earnestly assist them in having him as abbot. Fare well, reverend lord, and pray for us.

### Letter CXVI. Lambert to Lambert, Abbot

To the honourable lord, truly beloved and ever to be loved, LAMBERT, abbot, LAMBERT, however humble a servant of the holy Church of Arras he may be, and Archdeacons C. and R., lovers of your salvation and holiness: [Col. 0689D] eternal joy and gladness in the Holy Spirit, and to prefer nothing to the love of God.

Reverend lord and honoured Father, kindly do what we humbly ask of the wisdom divinely given you, for, according to the Apostle, “God loves a cheerful giver.” We desire humbly and effectually to obtain this: the brothers of Anchin have elected Alvisus, prior of Saint-Vaast. May it please you to grant him to them as abbot and restore him to us freed for obedience to our Church, so that in freedom of spirit he may preside over them and benefit them, and worthily serve God everywhere.

[Col. 0690A] For it is superfluous to teach you what blessed Benedict did with Saint Maurus; nor is it unknown to you what Saint Eustace, abbot, did with Saints Audomar, Bertin, and Mommolin: that all things may be done in charity, for love of God and affection for one’s neighbour; that others may be refreshed by the good fragrance of your monastery; and that good workers in the vineyard may through you be consoled. Fare well, beloved Father and lord, and pray for us.

### Letter CXVII. Baldric of Noyon to Lambert

To his lord and fellow brother LAMBERT, by God’s grace Bishop of Arras, BALDRIC, by the same grace Bishop of Noyon and Tournai: greeting and true love in Christ.

[Col. 0690B] We notify your brotherhood that this clerk named Bernard was born, raised, and educated in our diocese, and was promoted by us to the rank of priesthood. We send him to you as a free man, with due subjection and obedience, and lovingly ask that you grant him, with paternal kindness, the support of his office. Farewell.

### Letter CXVIII. Lambert to Odo of Cambrai

To the honourable Lord ODO, Bishop of Cambrai, LAMBERT, whatever manner of minister of the holy Church of Arras: the grace of spiritual joys.

It has been reported to us from the court, and through the court, of Baldwin, Count of Flanders, that you recently caused letters to be presented at Douai through your archdeacons A. and R. and the emperor’s messenger. Among other things, they contain this: “Therefore, by commanding request, we ask that you take care, for love of our favour, to support in every respect the Bishop of Cambrai and the Church entrusted to him in whatever that Church held in the district of Arras or in your county before the dispute between kingdom and priesthood.”

[Col. 0690C] In addition, one of the messengers named Estrées and Marœuil—matters not contained in the letters presented—and said that these and whatever else he wished belonged to the emperor.

But the Church of Arras and we, still unaware that Arras was of the Empire, but knowing it to be of the kingdom of the Franks; and since, by the counsel and aid of Count Robert, buried at the Castle, in whose power Arras was; and also by the permission and assent of Philip, King of the Franks, to whose realm Arras is known to belong; and through councils held at Reims under Archbishop Renaud; and by the authority of the Apostolic See and Pope Urban II of Rome, the entire proceeding concerning the Church of Arras was carried out and its establishment confirmed: it seems to us that you have acted irregularly toward us and toward the Church of Arras, in making complaint concerning us first through the courts of princes before summoning us through our common brethren and the suffragans of the province of Reims.

[Col. 0690D] We therefore ask you, by the love of brotherhood with which we sincerely love your holiness, to write back to us whether these aforesaid complaints were made by you before the princes. Fare well, and pray for us.

### Letter CXIX. Brother Wa. to Lambert

[Col. 0691A]

To the reverend lord and father LAMBERT, by God’s grace Bishop of the holy Church of Arras, Brother WA., servant of the servants of the Holy Trinity at Rouen, and the brothers entrusted to him: greeting and the service of due submission.

Reverently, lord, we offer thanks to the excellence of your dignity, because you have extended the kindness of your affection toward us so far that, even after the gift bestowed upon us by your favour, you confirmed that favour itself; and although we belong to another province, nevertheless, when the church of Ambrines was granted us, you wished us to be your parishioners. Therefore we devoutly offer you the devotion of our pious affection, and subject ourselves and all that is ours [Col. 0691B] to your command.

We willingly promise also to do for you as much as the right and custom due to the paternal dignity of the deceased lord abbot requires. For our lords, your canons, we have resolved to act in every respect as for our own brethren. We have appointed this brother of ours, R., over that same place of Ambrines, and command him to render to your dignity the obedience due. But all of us likewise wish to obey you in every submission as our Father and lord.

### Letter CXX

To the venerable Father and lord beloved in Christ Jesus, LAMBERT, by God’s grace Bishop of Arras, GODEFRID, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Amiens: to enjoy without end the joys of unending life.

[Col. 0691C] We gladly received the brothers from the titular church of Saint Mary in the Church of Arras and from the titular church of Saint-Vaast at the Castle, whom, reverend Father, you sent to our lowliness for promotion to holy orders. With the grace of the Holy Spirit cooperating, we have promoted them by the laying on of our hands and return them to your holiness: Hugh, Fulbert, Elbert, Hunold, and Arnulf to the order of priesthood; John, Adelelm, John, Robert, Gislebert, Odo, and Wicard to the order of the diaconate; Nicholas and Walter to the order of subdeacons. Farewell.

This was done in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1111, on the seventeenth day before the Kalends of April [16 March], in the fourth indiction.

### Letter CXXI. Lambert to Ivo of Chartres

[Col. 0691D] To the honourable lord and most beloved Father IVO, by God’s grace Bishop of Chartres, LAMBERT, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Arras: that which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor has entered into the heart of man.

Since it pleased your fatherhood both to greet us through the bearer of this letter and to send medicine for our illness, you have greatly gladdened us, since, placed amid such storms and oppressions of war, you remembered us. Since we cannot worthily return thanks to you as great as those we owe, may the almighty Lord and our Saviour Jesus Christ repay you at the resurrection of the just, because you have often done and continue to do many good things for us.

My reverend [Col. 0692A] Father and lord, fare well always in the Holy Spirit, and pray for me, a sinner, that almighty God, appeased by your holy prayers, may deign mercifully to absolve me, a sinner, from my sins, lead me from the darkness of this life and from the pit of misery, and establish me in the land of the living. Lord Clarembald, archdeacon, and Roger, deacon, most faithful lovers of your holiness, greet you warmly.

### Letter CXXII. Lambert to Godefrid of Amiens

To the beloved and ever to be loved Lord GODEFRID, by God’s grace Bishop of Amiens, LAMBERT, unprofitable servant of the holy Church of Arras: continual consolation in all things through the Holy Spirit.

[Col. 0692B] Guisfrid of Hamelaincourt and his brother Guy complain greatly to us that, although they first served you, you treat them as excommunicated, though they neither entered the church, nor removed a man captured there, nor even entered the churchyard, nor expect any share from his capture or ransom. They therefore urgently seek from us the judgment of the Church of Arras as to whether they ought to be excommunicated by you.

Likewise, Theodoric of Abling and his brother Guinemar, and our other parishioners of Pinchegny who joined Guarmund, complain that you have excommunicated them and that we mistreat them on that account. They seek judgment from us and our Church, since they are ready to swear that they knowingly possessed nothing belonging to you and that henceforth they will not serve Guarmund, [Col. 0692C] for fear of God and of you.

We send no answer concerning Hugh Campdavaine, because he neither resides nor is found in our diocese. Nevertheless, having received the counsel of our brethren and abbots, we dare in no way advise you to overstep the ancient boundaries which our fathers established in binding and loosing the people of God. Nor is it fitting for us, because of loss of property or money, to transgress in any respect the law of the Lord, which is without reproach. Fare well, and pray for us.

### Letter CXXIII. Lietard of Soissons to Lambert

To LAMBERT, by God’s grace Bishop of Arras, LIETARD, most humble Bishop of Soissons: happily to enjoy everlasting joy among the number of the elect.

[Col. 0692D] Since we received this Odo, brought up among us and raised to the rank of the lower orders, we promoted him to the priesthood, trusting in the testimony of his good character. We therefore entrust to your care this aforesaid priest and whatever lay within our jurisdiction. Farewell.

### Letter CXXIV. Ralph of Reims to Lambert

RALPH, by God’s grace Archbishop of Reims, to his venerable brother and fellow bishop LAMBERT of Arras: greeting.

Persons coming to us from the Church of Laon reported that, by the common will of the whole clergy, the request of the people, and royal assent, [Col. 0693A] they had elected Lord Hugh, dean of the Church of Orléans, as bishop. They hoped in God’s mercy that, through him, relief could be brought both to the desolation of their Church and to the calamity of their city and country; and, repeatedly and urgently petitioning us, they demanded that we should delay their elect’s consecration no longer.

Accordingly, we summoned our fellow brethren and fellow bishops to Reims for his consecration on the day before the Nones of August [4 August], and we would be greatly consoled if you were present with them. But because illness prevents us and we despair of being able to attend, we entrust to the discretion of your brotherhood that, as the authority of the holy Fathers requires, you arrange to send your assent for the consecration of the aforesaid elect. Farewell.

### Letter CXXV. Lambert to Ralph

[Col. 0693B]

To the reverend Father and lord RALPH, by God’s appointment Archbishop of Reims, LAMBERT, whatever manner of minister of the Church of Arras: the grace of spiritual joys.

Concerning Lord Hugh, dean of the Church of Orléans and now elect of the Church of Laon, regarding whom you wished, as is canonical, to have our assent: we reply to your fatherhood in this letter from our lowliness that whatever your metropolitan authority judges concerning his consecration, and does in the Lord’s name according to the decrees of the holy Fathers, we shall gladly give our assent to it; and we earnestly desire that almighty God by his grace make him worthy [Col. 0693C] of it. Fare well, reverend Father and lord, with all gathered at Reims in the Holy Spirit; and pray for us.

### Letter CXXVI. To Baldwin, Count of Flanders

LAMBERT, by God’s mercy Bishop of Arras, to BALDWIN, honourable and magnificent Count of the Flemings: help and counsel always from the Lord God.

Your mother, Countess Clementia, complains concerning her dower lands and the other possessions which your father conveyed to her and permitted her peacefully to possess, that you likewise permit her to possess those same [lacuna] possessions peacefully and without disturbance. [Col. 0693D] We therefore ask your excellence not to provoke your mother to anger, but to support her gently, according to the command of the Lord who said: “Honour your father and your mother, that you may be long-lived upon the land which the Lord your God will give you,” so that you may live long from the Lord and as a prince of peace upon the earth.

But if you are unwilling to do this, she asks us, and we ask at her request on her behalf, that you appoint a day for her, summon the counts of your land and the castellans whom she wishes to be present in this case, and she is prepared to abide by whatever they judge for her in your court or in the court of the King of the Franks. Farewell.

### Letter CXXVII. Lambert to Eustace, Count of Boulogne

LAMBERT, by God’s mercy Bishop of Arras, [Col. 0694A] to his beloved and honourable parishioner EUSTACE, Count of Boulogne: eternal salvation in the Lord God.

We ask you to release and make safe the knight captured at Nielle, to whom the Lord gave refuge in the church of Blessed Mary ever Virgin, our Lady; to honour the Church of God; and to preserve your castle in freedom of spirit. And, because we have heard that the Count of Flanders is at Lens, we order through you and entreat him by this present letter to permit the same knight to depart safely through his land. For there is no one among you, rich or poor, who, in danger of death or capture, would flee to a church and not wish to be freed through the Church. Fare well, do the things that are God’s, and God will do the things [Col. 0694B] that are yours.

### Letter CXXVIII. Lambert to Ralph of Reims

To the reverend Father and lord RALPH, by God’s mercy Archbishop of Reims, and to all honourable bishops and abbots assembled at Reims in the name of Jesus, LAMBERT, whatever manner of minister of the holy Church of Arras: discipline and wisdom in the Holy Spirit.

Since it pleased you, reverend Father, to instruct us, concerning the complaint of our canons and of Lord Henry, abbot of Saint-Vaast, and the monks, that the abbot’s summons should be deferred until the Kalends of November, it has been done as you commanded and approved by both parties. Fare well, reverend [Col. 0694C] Father and honourable bishops, my lords, with all assembled in council; pray for me, a sinner; and work earnestly so that we may rejoice, through you, in having obtained for our Churches—not the peace which the world can give, but that peace which surpasses all understanding, namely that of angels and men—by God’s mercy and the cooperation of the Holy Spirit.

### Letter CXXIX. Gualo of Paris to Lambert

To his lord and friend LAMBERT, by God’s grace Bishop of Arras, GUALO, priest of Paris: greeting.

As you stated in your letter, that every Church ought to agree with the holy Roman, Catholic, and Apostolic Church in faith, in the celebration of the sacraments, and in observing the canonical hours according to the institution of the orthodox Fathers, I have taken care, as you requested, to set down in this letter whatever, while at Rome, I saw, heard, and could recall concerning these matters.

[Col. 0694D] The Roman clergy are not accustomed at any time—whether in Advent, vigils, or Lent—to say prayers at Prime, Sext, and None; but after the chapter, responsory, verse, *Kyrie eleison*, *Christe eleison*, *Kyrie eleison*, they immediately say the collect without the *Pater noster*. They do this also on all feasts.

At Matins and Vespers only, prostrate, they say the *Pater noster* with the chapters of “Have mercy on me, O God”; but after the *Kyrie eleison* has been repeated three times, *Benedicamus Domino* follows. Know, finally, that the pope observes in his private chapel the same custom observed by regular canons in these regions, except that on festal days within octaves the *Kyrie eleison* is said three times before the collect.

[Col. 0695A] On the night of the Lord’s Nativity, however, without “Lord, open my lips,” without “O God, make haste to help me,” and without the invitatory, beginning with an antiphon and psalm, they perform nine lessons, which they call the Vigil. When the ninth lesson has ended, they say the collect without a responsory and without Lauds.

Know also that the Romans never sing a responsory after the ninth lesson on feast days, but immediately begin “We praise thee, O God.” Likewise, on other days they do not say a responsory after the third lesson; but, once the verse has been said, “O God, make haste to help me” follows, together with the other things to be said at Matins Lauds. [Col. 0695B] I think this custom grew up because they were accustomed always to expound the final lesson to the people.

After the Vigil on the night of the Nativity of the Lord, mentioned above, they celebrate Matins as we do, and insert the first Mass as we do. From the Sunday on which “Judge me, O God” is sung as the Introit, they do not say “Glory be to the Father,” just as neither do we. At the Lord’s Supper, they conclude the daytime hours without antiphon or responsory as follows: the one presiding in choir says, “Christ became obedient for us to the Father unto death.” On Good Friday there is added, “even death on a cross.” On Holy Saturday there is added, “Therefore God also exalted him and gave him the name which is above every name.”

[Col. 0695C] We have answered these things briefly, insofar as they came to mind. Should God grant us the conversation which we desire, we shall fully explain, according to your inquiry, the remaining matters which are not within your knowledge, once they have been examined.

### Letter CXXX. Robert of Nantes to Lambert

To the venerable LAMBERT, Bishop of Arras, ROBERT, Bishop of Nantes: the joys of eternal life.

We have heard that a certain countryman of ours, named Thietbold, departed for foreign parts for the sake of study and is at present residing among you. Certain persons of your region, as has been reported to us, prompted by envy, accuse him of falsehood: some say that he was a monk; others that he became implicated in [Col. 0695D] homicide; others, indeed, that he committed some such act as would render him liable to exile. We therefore make known and attest to Your Excellency, under truthful testimony, that he is not only unentangled in the aforesaid crimes, but was legitimately born, descended from noble lay parents, and involved in no criminal matter that should prevent his advancement to the highest rank of whatever dignity.

Moreover, that the tongues of detractors and envious persons may be silenced concerning him, we commend him and grant permission for him to be ordained by any Catholic bishop, with this testimonial letter. To remove every ambiguity entirely, we have inserted in it the first Greek-written letters of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit—Π, Υ, Α; likewise the first letter of the name of the apostle Peter [Col. 0696A], Π; the first letter of my own name, Ρ; the second of yours, Α; the third of the name of him whom we commend, Θ; the fourth of our city, Ν; and the fifth of the indiction, whose present number is Ε short. Collected together, these complete the number 753. We have also added the number 98, which, according to Greek letters, signifies ΑΜΗΝ, “Amen.”

## LETTERS CXXXVI–CXXXVIII OF POPE PASCHAL TO LAMBERT

(See among Paschal’s letters, *Patrologia*, vol. CLXIII, [Col. 0696D] nos. 369, 370, 249.)

## LETTER CXXXIX. OF LAMBERT TO HENRY OF SAINT-VAAST, ALBERT OF HASNON, AND FULCARD OF MARCHIENNES

LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras, to his beloved brothers and abbots in Christ—HENRY of Saint-Vaast, ALBERT of Hasnon, and FULCARD of Marchiennes—may they attain eternal joy through the obedience that is in Christ.

We wish Your Affection to know that the bishop of Thérouanne and we have recently received letters from the apostolic see, commanding us to appoint for the canons of the holy Church of Tournai and the monks of the monastery of Saint Martin at Tournai a day and place [Col. 0697A] where, after a careful hearing of the complaint long disputed between them, we should endeavour, appeals being set aside, to bring it through God’s grace to its proper conclusion.

Therefore, although unwillingly, because of fear arising from our grave and prolonged illness, yet receiving charge of this affair by apostolic authority, we likewise command and enjoin Your Fraternity by that authority that, setting aside every excuse, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of August, before the third hour of the day, you do not fail to be present with us at the castle of Capi, belonging to the valiant knight Lord Robert of Péronne, to give counsel and aid in the causes of the holy Roman Church. Fare well always in the Lord, and pray for us.

## LETTER CXL. OF THE SAME TO SIGER, ABBOT OF TOURNAI

[Col. 0697B] LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras, to his beloved brother in Christ SIGER, abbot of the monastery of Tournai, and to the whole community entrusted to him: may you always walk in the paths of justice and please God in all your deeds.

We wish Your Affection to know that we have recently received letters from the apostolic see commanding us to appoint for you and the canons of the holy Church of Tournai a day and place where, after carefully hearing the complaint long disputed between you and the aforesaid canons, we should endeavour, appeals being set aside, to bring it to its proper conclusion. Therefore, by the same authority of the apostolic see by which—although unwillingly, owing to fear of our grave and prolonged illness—we are constrained to do this, we admonish and command you not to delay being present on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of August [Col. 0697C], before the third hour of the day, at the castle of Capi, belonging to the valiant knight Lord Robert of Péronne. Fare well, and pray for us.

## LETTER CXLI. TO GOTHER, DEAN OF TOURNAI, AND G., PROVOST

LAMBERT, by God’s mercy bishop of Arras, to his beloved brothers in Christ, Lord GOTHER, dean of the Church of Tournai, and G., provost: eternal salvation in the Lord.

Although recently, from fear caused by our grave and prolonged illness, we unwillingly undertook to hear your complaint, long pending between you and the monks of the monastery of Saint Martin at Tournai, yet now at last constrained by the authority of the apostolic see, we command and enjoin you to ensure that you present yourselves for the hearing of your case on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of August, before the third hour of the day, at the castle of Capi, belonging to the valiant knight Lord Robert of Péronne. [Col. 0697D] Fare well, and pray for us.

## LETTER CXLII. OF THE BRETHREN OF THE CHURCH OF TOURNAI TO LAMBERT

To their lord, Lord LAMBERT, by God’s providence bishop of the Church of Arras: the venerable GOTHER, dean, together with the other brethren of the Church of Tournai, offers the support of prayers and the services of fidelity that is not undue.

Our church, not forgetting with what kindly and fatherly affection you assisted us in the case which we had against the monks [Col. 0698A] of Saint Martin, renders fitting thanks to Your Fatherhood. But because we fear that we and our possessions may be attacked in the future, we earnestly beseech Your Holiness and ask that you confirm for us in writing and by the authority of your seal the manner in which the decree of your judgment ended the dispute between us and the monks. Farewell.

## LETTER CXLIII. Agreement between the Canons of Tournai and the Monks of Saint Martin

In the name of the one true and supreme God, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. Amen.
